# Route reference

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/routes

Every framework adapter wraps one handler from core, `createTheAuthHandler` in `@glinr/theauth/http`, so every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. Paths are relative to the mount path (default `/api/theauth`).

```typescript
import { createTheAuthHandler } from '@glinr/theauth/http';

const handler = createTheAuthHandler(theauth, { mcp, basePath: '/api/theauth' });
// handler: (request: Request) => Promise<Response>
```

## Routes

| Method | Path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/agents` | admin | List agents (filters: userId, status, type) |
| `POST` | `/agents` | admin | Create an agent |
| `GET` | `/agents/:id` | admin | Get an agent |
| `PATCH` | `/agents/:id` | admin | Update an agent |
| `DELETE` | `/agents/:id` | admin | Revoke an agent |
| `POST` | `/agents/:id/rotate` | admin | Rotate an agent token |
| `POST` | `/authorize` | admin | Check whether an agent may perform an action (403 when denied) |
| `POST` | `/authorize/token` | agent | Check an action using the agent bearer token (401 bad token, 403 denied) |
| `POST` | `/delegations` | admin | Delegate permissions from one agent to another |
| `GET` | `/delegations/:id` | admin | List delegation chains of an agent (id is the agent id) |
| `DELETE` | `/delegations/:id` | admin | Revoke a delegation chain (id is the chain id) |
| `GET` | `/audit` | admin | Query audit entries |
| `GET` | `/audit/export` | admin | Export audit entries as JSON or CSV |
| `GET` | `/dashboard/stats` | admin | Dashboard aggregates |
| `GET` | `/dashboard/agents` | admin | Dashboard agent list (same as GET /agents) |
| `GET` | `/dashboard/audit` | admin | Dashboard audit list (same as GET /audit) |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | public | OAuth authorization server metadata (RFC 8414) |
| `GET` | `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` | public | Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) |
| `POST` | `/mcp/register` | public | Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) |
| `GET` | `/mcp/authorize` | public | Authorization endpoint (redirects to login or the client) |
| `POST` | `/mcp/token` | client | Token endpoint |
| `POST` | `/mcp/revoke` | client | Token revocation (RFC 7009) |
| `POST` | `/mcp/introspect` | client | Token introspection (RFC 7662), 404 until `introspection.enabled` |
| `GET` | `/mcp/jwks` | public | Public signing keys (JWKS) |
| `POST` | `/explain` | admin | Explain an authorization decision without recording it |

Generated from `listRoutes()`. Call it yourself to render the table or build an OpenAPI document:

```typescript
import { listRoutes } from '@glinr/theauth/http';

for (const route of listRoutes({ routes: { explain: false } })) {
  console.log(route.method, route.path, route.auth);
}
```

### Auth levels

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `admin` | A signed-in user (cookie or `Authorization: Bearer <session token>`), or the principal your `authenticate` option returns. With the default session resolver a user only sees and changes their own agents, delegations and audit rows. |
| `agent` | An agent bearer token (`Authorization: Bearer ta_...`). |
| `client` | An OAuth client. Credentials travel in the request (client secret, `private_key_jwt` assertion). |
| `public` | No credentials. The route validates its own input. |

## Status codes

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| 200, 201, 204 | Success (create answers 201, revoke and delete answer 204) |
| 400 | Invalid JSON, failed validation, bad query value |
| 401 | No or invalid credentials. Agent identity failures (`invalid_token`, `agent_not_found`, `agent_revoked`, `agent_expired`) are 401 |
| 403 | Authenticated but not allowed: a denied authorization, a cross-owner filter, or a failed cross-site check (`CSRF_REJECTED`) |
| 404 | Unknown route, a resource you do not own (existence is not revealed), or an MCP route that is not mounted |
| 405 | Known path, wrong method (an `Allow` header lists the methods) |
| 413 | Body larger than `maxBodyBytes` |
| 429 | Rate limited (`Retry-After` is set) |

Management errors use `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`. MCP endpoints use the OAuth shape `{ "error", "error_description" }`.

## Options

`createTheAuthHandler(theauth, options)` takes the shared security options plus:

| Option | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `mcp` | none | MCP module. Without it the MCP and well-known routes answer 404. |
| `basePath` | `/api/theauth` | Mount prefix. |
| `routes.management` | `true` | Agents, delegations, audit, dashboard, authorize. |
| `routes.mcp` | `true` | MCP and well-known routes. Pass an object such as `{ revoke: false, jwks: false }` to mount a subset. Metadata lists only what is mounted. |
| `routes.plugins` | `true` | Fall through to plugin endpoints. |
| `routes.explain` | `true` | `POST /explain`. |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `1048576` | Request body limit. |
| `securityHeaders` | off | Response hardening headers. `true` for defaults or an options object. See [Security headers](#security-headers). |
| `cors` | off | Exact-origin allowlist. See [CORS](#cors). |
| `authenticate`, `allowUnauthenticated`, `trustedProxy`, `rateLimit`, `trustedOrigins`, `csrf` | | Same meaning as in [adapter security](/adapters). |

## Cache headers

Every response the handler produces carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Pragma: no-cache`, because auth responses hold credentials or session state: tokens, introspection results, authorize redirects, errors from guarded routes and anything that sets a cookie. The default is applied in one place; a route that sets its own `Cache-Control` keeps it (`GET /mcp/jwks` stays `public, max-age=300`). A 404 for a path the handler does not own is left alone.

## Security headers

Off by default. Pass `securityHeaders: true` (or an options object) to add:

| Header | Value | Sent on |
|---|---|---|
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff` | every response |
| `Referrer-Policy` | `no-referrer` (tokens in magic-link and reset URLs never leak) | every response |
| `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` | `same-origin` | every response |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` | https requests only |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` | HTML responses only |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | `default-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'` | HTML responses only |

HSTS is sent when the request URL is https, or when `trustedProxy` is configured and the proxy reports `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`. Without `trustedProxy` the forwarded header is ignored, so a client cannot trigger it. The core routes return JSON, so frame and CSP headers matter for HTML that plugins return. A header the route already set is never overwritten. Each header takes an override or `false` (`hsts`, `referrerPolicy`, `frameOptions`, `contentSecurityPolicy`, `crossOriginResourcePolicy`).

For responses you build yourself:

```typescript
import { securityHeaders, isSecureRequest } from '@glinr/theauth/http';

return new Response(html, {
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'text/html',
    ...securityHeaders({ html: true, secure: isSecureRequest(request, { trustedProxyCount: 1 }) }),
  },
});
```

## CORS

Off by default: no CORS header is sent anywhere. (Earlier versions sent `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every MCP route, token endpoint included.) Browser based MCP clients need the discovery documents, so list the origins that may read them:

```typescript
createTheAuthHandler(theauth, {
  mcp,
  cors: { origins: ['https://app.example.com'] },
});
```

Rules, all enforced:

- Origins are matched exactly (scheme, host, port). An origin that is not listed gets no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`; it is never reflected. `Vary: Origin` is always set when a group has an allowlist.
- `"*"` is accepted only for public documents. It cannot be combined with `credentials: true`, and cannot be used for `token`, `introspect`, `revoke` or `management`: the handler throws at startup.
- A preflight (`OPTIONS` with `Access-Control-Request-Method`) is answered before authentication. It lists the methods that path serves, `allowedHeaders` (default `Content-Type, Authorization, DPoP`) and `maxAge` (default 600 seconds). A disallowed origin or method gets a bare 204.
- `exposedHeaders` defaults to `DPoP-Nonce, WWW-Authenticate`.

| Group | Routes | Default once `origins` is set |
|---|---|---|
| `discovery` | both `/.well-known/*` documents, `/mcp/jwks` | on |
| `register` | `/mcp/register` | off |
| `token` | `/mcp/token` | off |
| `introspect` | `/mcp/introspect` | off |
| `revoke` | `/mcp/revoke` | off |
| `management` | agents, delegations, audit, dashboard, authorize/token, explain | off |

`/mcp/authorize` is a browser navigation and never gets CORS. Opt a group in with `groups: { token: true }` (uses `origins`) or `groups: { token: ['https://spa.example.com'] }` (its own list). Token, introspection and revoke are client credential endpoints for servers; enable them for a browser only for a public client you control.

At startup the handler logs a warning through the observability logger (console when none is set) when `allowUnauthenticated` is on, or when CORS allows `"*"` or opens a credential carrying group.

## Guarding your own routes

`requireAgent` authenticates an agent token and checks one action. It never compares reason strings, it branches on the decision code.

```typescript
import { requireAgent } from '@glinr/theauth/http';

const result = await requireAgent(theauth, request, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' });
if (!result.ok) return result.response; // 401 or 403, body { error: { code, message } }
result.agent; // identity without the token
```

| Decision code | Status |
|---|---|
| `invalid_token`, `agent_not_found`, `agent_revoked`, `agent_expired` | 401 |
| every other denial (`no_permission`, `rate_limited`, `ip_not_allowed`, `approval_required`, ...) | 403 |

## Node bridge

Express, Fastify and NestJS use Node's `http` objects. `toWebRequest(req, { trustProxy })` and `sendWebResponse(res, response)` convert both ways, so those adapters are a few lines around the same handler.

## Client IP and peer address

The client IP feeds per-IP rate limits, `ipAllowlist` permissions and audit rows. It is resolved in one place:

- With `trustedProxy` set (`trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`), the proxy headers decide, exactly as before.
- Without it, forwarded headers are ignored and the socket's remote address is used.

`toWebRequest` records the socket address on the `Request` out of band (never in a header, so a client cannot spoof it). Read it with `peerAddressOf(request)` from `@glinr/theauth/http`. Express, Fastify and NestJS therefore have a client IP on a direct deployment. Web-standard frameworks (Hono, Next.js and similar) never go through `toWebRequest`, so they still need `trustedProxy` to know the IP. `requireAgent` uses the same resolver when `clientIp` is not given; pass `trustedProxy` to it when you run behind a proxy.

## Owner filters

A caller limited to their own resources gets `403` with `{ error: { code: "FORBIDDEN", message } }` when `userId` names someone else, on `GET /audit/export`, `GET /audit`, `GET /agents` and the dashboard lists. The filter is never silently dropped.

---

# Hono

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/hono

`theAuthHono(theauth, options?)` returns a `Hono` app instance with all theAuth routes pre-mounted. Use `app.route` to attach it to your main app.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-hono hono @hono/node-server
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

Create this once and reuse it across your app (e.g. `lib/theauth.ts`):

```typescript
// lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'sqlite-native', url: 'theauth.db' },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Mount the adapter">

```typescript
// src/index.ts
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { theAuthHono } from '@glinr/theauth-hono';
import { theauth, mcp } from './lib/theauth.js';

const app = new Hono();

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

// Mount all TheAuth routes (agents, permissions, audit, MCP OAuth)
app.route('/api/theauth', theAuthHono(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));

serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: 3000 });
```

</Step>
</Steps>

## Authentication and mount prefixes

`theAuthHono` refuses to start without a way to authenticate callers on `/agents`, `/delegations`, `/audit`, `/dashboard` and `POST /authorize`. Pass `authenticate`, configure `auth.session`, or set `allowUnauthenticated: true` for local development. The full rules and the upgrade note are on the [adapters overview](/adapters#authenticate-the-management-routes).

```typescript
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

app.route('/api/theauth', theAuthHono(theauth, { authenticate }));
```

Plugin routes (magic link, email OTP and so on) work under any prefix. The adapter works out the prefix from the request path, so `app.route('/x', theAuthHono(...))` and `app.route('/api/v1/theauth', ...)` both reach `/auth/magic-link/send` at the right place.

## MCP endpoints

Pass `mcp` to enable the full MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server. All MCP endpoints are mounted under the same `/api/theauth` prefix alongside the REST API:

```typescript
app.route('/api/theauth', theAuthHono(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));
// registers:
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
// GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
```

<Info>
  MCP routes include CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`) and respond to OPTIONS preflight requests automatically.
</Info>

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
app.route('/api/theauth', theAuthHono(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } }));
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

Every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. See the [route reference](/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route for agents

```typescript
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { requireScope, type AgentEnv } from '@glinr/theauth-hono';

const app = new Hono<AgentEnv>();
app.get('/invoices', requireScope(theauth, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' }), (c) =>
  c.json({ agentId: c.get('agent').id }),
);
```

Missing or invalid bearer token returns 401 and a denied scope returns 403. The body is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, where `code` is the decision code (for example `no_permission`). See the [requireScope guide](/require-scope).

## Full example

```typescript
import { serve } from '@hono/node-server';
import { Hono } from 'hono';
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page
import { theAuthHono } from '@glinr/theauth-hono';

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'sqlite-native', url: 'theauth.db' },
  baseUrl: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: 'https://auth.yourapp.com',
    baseUrl: 'https://auth.yourapp.com/api/theauth',
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});

const app = new Hono();

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

app.route('/api/theauth', theAuthHono(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));

app.get('/health', (c) => c.json({ ok: true }));

serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: 3000 });
```

# Elysia

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/elysia

Elysia mounts any function of the shape `(request: Request) => Response | Promise<Response>`, which is what `createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http` returns. So there is no Elysia package: you use the core handler directly.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth elysia
```

## Mount the handler

`app.mount(prefix, handler)` strips the prefix before calling the handler, so pass `basePath: ""`.

```typescript
import { Elysia } from "elysia";
import { createTheAuth } from "@glinr/theauth";
import { createTheAuthHandler, requireAgent } from "@glinr/theauth/http";

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: "sqlite", url: ":memory:" },
  agents: { enabled: true, maxPerUser: 10, defaultPermissions: [], auditAll: true },
});

const handler = createTheAuthHandler(theauth, {
  basePath: "",
  // Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null for a 401.
  authenticate: async (request) => {
    const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
    return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
  },
});

const app = new Elysia()
  .mount("/api/theauth", handler)
  .get("/docs", async ({ request }) => {
    const result = await requireAgent(theauth, request, { action: "read", resource: "docs" });
    if (!result.ok) return result.response; // 401 or 403 with { error: { code, message } }
    return { agentId: result.agent.id };
  });

export default app;
```

`requireAgent` is the same decision logic the Hono, Express and Fastify `requireScope` helpers use.

## What was run

This snippet type checks under `strict` against Elysia 1.4 and was run with `app.handle`: `GET /api/theauth/agents` answered 200 with an authenticated caller, `GET /docs` without a token answered 401, and an unknown path under the mount answered 404.

---

# Nitro

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/nitro

A Nitro route handler can return the `Response` that `createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http` produces, so there is no Nitro package. This page is for a standalone Nitro server, or any app that uses Nitro without Nuxt. In a Nuxt app use [`@glinr/theauth-nuxt`](/adapters/nuxt), which wraps the same handler.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth better-sqlite3
pnpm add nitro        # Nitro 3 (beta)
# or: pnpm add nitropack   # Nitro 2
```

Nitro 3 beta needs `pg` and `mysql2` installed as well, even if you never use them. Its bundler hoists the lazy driver imports in `drizzle-orm` into one chunk that imports both at startup, so a missing package fails the first request. Nitro 2 does not do this.

## Create the instance once

Nitro 2 builds for `es2019`, which has no top-level `await`. Create the instance on the first request and reuse it. This works on Nitro 2 and 3.

```typescript title="server/utils/theauth.ts"
import { createTheAuth } from "@glinr/theauth";
import { createTheAuthHandler } from "@glinr/theauth/http";

async function setup() {
  const theauth = await createTheAuth({
    database: { provider: "sqlite-native", url: "theauth.db" },
    agents: { enabled: true, maxPerUser: 10, defaultPermissions: [], auditAll: true },
  });
  const handler = createTheAuthHandler(theauth, {
    basePath: "/api/theauth",
    // Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null for a 401.
    authenticate: async (request) => {
      const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
      return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
    },
  });
  return { theauth, handler };
}

let instance: ReturnType<typeof setup> | undefined;

export function useTheAuth() {
  instance ??= setup();
  return instance;
}
```

The in-memory `sql.js` provider (`provider: "sqlite"`) does not survive a Nitro 3 build: the bundler inlines its CommonJS file and the first request fails with `__dirname is not defined`. Use `sqlite-native`, Postgres or D1.

## Mount the handler

The route file is a catch-all. The handler sees the full path, so `basePath` is the mount path.

<CodeGroup>

```typescript title="Nitro 3: server/routes/api/theauth/[...path].ts"
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
import { useTheAuth } from "../../../utils/theauth";

export default defineHandler(async (event) => {
  const { handler } = await useTheAuth();
  return handler(event.req); // event.req is a Web Request
});
```

```typescript title="Nitro 2: server/routes/api/theauth/[...path].ts"
import { toWebRequest } from "h3";
import { useTheAuth } from "../../../utils/theauth";

export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const { handler } = await useTheAuth();
  return handler(toWebRequest(event));
});
```

</CodeGroup>

## Protect your own routes

`requireAgent` is the decision logic behind the `requireScope` helpers of the other adapters. It returns the agent, or a ready 401 or 403 `Response`.

```typescript title="Nitro 3: server/routes/docs.get.ts"
import { defineHandler } from "nitro";
import { requireAgent } from "@glinr/theauth/http";
import { useTheAuth } from "../utils/theauth";

export default defineHandler(async (event) => {
  const { theauth } = await useTheAuth();
  const result = await requireAgent(theauth, event.req, { action: "read", resource: "docs" });
  if (!result.ok) return result.response; // 401 or 403 with { error: { code, message } }
  return { agentId: result.agent.id };
});
```

On Nitro 2 pass `toWebRequest(event)` instead of `event.req`.

## What was run

Both versions were built with `nitro build` and `nitropack build` and started from the build output, with `@glinr/theauth` installed from a packed tarball (so the bundler treated it like an installed dependency). On Nitro 3 beta (`3.0.260903-beta`, h3 2.0.5) and Nitro 2: `GET /api/theauth/agents` without a session answered 401, an unknown path under the mount answered 404, and `GET /docs` without a token answered 401. With an `authenticate` stub that accepts a test header, `GET /api/theauth/agents` answered 200. The `sql.js` and missing `pg` and `mysql2` failures above come from those runs.

# Waku

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/waku

Waku API routes export functions named after HTTP methods. Each takes a Web `Request` and returns a `Response`, which is what `createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http` produces. There is no Waku package.

API routes live in `src/pages/_api`. The `_api` directory is not part of the URL, so `src/pages/_api/theauth/[...path].ts` answers at `/theauth/*`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth better-sqlite3 waku react react-dom react-server-dom-webpack
```

## Create the instance once

```typescript title="src/lib/theauth.ts"
import { createTheAuth } from "@glinr/theauth";
import { createTheAuthHandler } from "@glinr/theauth/http";

async function setup() {
  const theauth = await createTheAuth({
    database: { provider: "sqlite-native", url: "theauth.db" },
    agents: { enabled: true, maxPerUser: 10, defaultPermissions: [], auditAll: true },
  });
  const handler = createTheAuthHandler(theauth, {
    basePath: "/theauth",
    // Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null for a 401.
    authenticate: async (request) => {
      const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
      return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
    },
  });
  return { theauth, handler };
}

let instance: ReturnType<typeof setup> | undefined;

export function useTheAuth() {
  instance ??= setup();
  return instance;
}
```

## Mount the handler

```typescript title="src/pages/_api/theauth/[...path].ts"
import { useTheAuth } from "../../../lib/theauth";

const serve = async (request: Request): Promise<Response> => {
  const { handler } = await useTheAuth();
  return handler(request);
};

export const GET = serve;
export const POST = serve;
export const PUT = serve;
export const PATCH = serve;
export const DELETE = serve;
```

API routes are dynamic by default, so no `getConfig` is needed.

## Keep native packages out of the bundle

Waku builds with Vite and Rolldown and bundles server dependencies. Two things then break: `better-sqlite3` fails with `__dirname is not defined` on the first request, and `@glinr/theauth` carries an optional `nodemailer` import that Rolldown refuses to leave unresolved. Mark both external:

```typescript title="waku.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "waku/config";

export default defineConfig({
  vite: {
    build: {
      rolldownOptions: {
        // Native and optional packages stay in node_modules instead of being bundled.
        external: ["better-sqlite3", "nodemailer"],
      },
    },
  },
});
```

If you use the email adapters or another optional driver, add its package name to `external` the same way. With Postgres you would externalize `pg` instead of `better-sqlite3`.

## Protect your own routes

```typescript title="src/pages/_api/docs.ts"
import { requireAgent } from "@glinr/theauth/http";
import { useTheAuth } from "../../lib/theauth";

export const GET = async (request: Request): Promise<Response> => {
  const { theauth } = await useTheAuth();
  const result = await requireAgent(theauth, request, { action: "read", resource: "docs" });
  if (!result.ok) return result.response; // 401 or 403 with { error: { code, message } }
  return Response.json({ agentId: result.agent.id });
};
```

## What was run

A scratch Waku project (`waku@1.0.0-rc.3`, React 19.3, Node 22) with `@glinr/theauth` installed from a packed tarball. After `waku build` and `waku start`: `GET /theauth/agents` without a session answered 401, an unknown path under the mount answered 404, and `GET /docs` without a token answered 401. Both failures described above were reproduced before the config was added. The session cookie flow for pages (server components reading the session) was not run.

# React Router

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/react-router

React Router v7 (and Remix) resource routes receive a Web `Request` and return a `Response`, so the core handler fits with no wrapper package.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth
```

## Resource route

Create `app/routes/api.theauth.$.ts` and register it with `route("api/theauth/*", "routes/api.theauth.$.ts")` in `app/routes.ts`. The request keeps its full path, so leave `basePath` at the default `/api/theauth`.

```typescript
// app/routes/api.theauth.$.ts
import { createTheAuthHandler } from "@glinr/theauth/http";
import { theauth } from "~/lib/theauth.server";

const handler = createTheAuthHandler(theauth, {
  authenticate: async (request) => {
    const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
    return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
  },
});

export const loader = ({ request }: { request: Request }) => handler(request);
export const action = ({ request }: { request: Request }) => handler(request);
```

Export both `loader` (GET, HEAD) and `action` (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Build the handler once at module scope so an unsafe configuration fails at startup.

## What was run

The handler contract (full path in, `Response` out and 404 outside the base path) is covered by `packages/core/tests/http/fetch-mount.test.ts`. This page did not run a React Router app.

---

# Express

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/express

`theAuthExpress(theauth, options?)` returns an Express `Router` with all theAuth routes pre-mounted. Use `app.use` to attach it at your chosen path.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-express express
pnpm add -D @types/express
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

```typescript
// lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Mount the adapter">

```typescript
// src/index.ts
import express from 'express';
import { theAuthExpress } from '@glinr/theauth-express';
import { theauth, mcp } from './lib/theauth.js';

const app = express();

// Required: parse JSON and URL-encoded bodies before the adapter
app.use(express.json());
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

// Mount all TheAuth routes
app.use('/api/theauth', theAuthExpress(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));

app.listen(3000);
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
  Call `express.json()` and `express.urlencoded()` before mounting the adapter. The adapter reads `req.body` which requires those parsers to be in place.
</Warning>

## MCP endpoints

Pass `mcp` to enable the MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server. All MCP endpoints are registered on the same router alongside the REST API:

```typescript
app.use('/api/theauth', theAuthExpress(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));
// registers:
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
// GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
```

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
app.use('/api/theauth', theAuthExpress(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } }));
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

Every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. See the [route reference](/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route for agents

```typescript
import { getAgent, requireScope } from '@glinr/theauth-express';

app.get('/invoices', requireScope(theauth, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' }), (_req, res) => {
  res.json({ agentId: getAgent(res)?.id });
});
```

Missing or invalid bearer token returns 401 and a denied scope returns 403. The body is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, where `code` is the decision code (for example `no_permission`). See the [requireScope guide](/require-scope).

## Full example

```typescript
import express from 'express';
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page
import { theAuthExpress } from '@glinr/theauth-express';

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.use(express.urlencoded({ extended: true }));

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

app.use('/api/theauth', theAuthExpress(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }));

app.get('/health', (_req, res) => res.json({ ok: true }));

app.listen(3000, () => {
  console.log('Server running on port 3000');
});
```

# Fastify

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/fastify

`theAuthFastify(theauth, options?)` returns an async Fastify plugin. Register it with `fastify.register` and use Fastify's built-in `prefix` option to control the mount path.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-fastify fastify
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

```typescript
// lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Register the plugin">

```typescript
// src/index.ts
import Fastify from 'fastify';
import { theAuthFastify } from '@glinr/theauth-fastify';
import { theauth, mcp } from './lib/theauth.js';

const app = Fastify();

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

// Use Fastify's prefix option to set the mount path
await app.register(theAuthFastify(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }), {
  prefix: '/api/theauth',
});

await app.listen({ port: 3000 });
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  The prefix is controlled by Fastify's `register` options, and the handler picks it up. You can still pass `basePath` to override it.
</Info>

## MCP endpoints

When `mcp` is passed, the MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints are registered on the same plugin. Because Fastify's prefix scopes routes, the well-known paths are served relative to the plugin root:

```
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
```

All MCP routes include CORS headers and respond to OPTIONS preflight requests.

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
await app.register(theAuthFastify(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } }), { prefix: '/api/theauth' });
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites. Without `trustedProxy` the adapter uses `request.ip`, which is the socket peer unless your server framework is configured to trust the proxy.

## Endpoint reference

Every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. See the [route reference](/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route for agents

```typescript
import { getAgent, requireScope } from '@glinr/theauth-fastify';

app.get(
  '/invoices',
  { preHandler: requireScope(theauth, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' }) },
  async (request) => ({ agentId: getAgent(request)?.id }),
);
```

Missing or invalid bearer token returns 401 and a denied scope returns 403. The body is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, where `code` is the decision code (for example `no_permission`). See the [requireScope guide](/require-scope).

## Full example

```typescript
import Fastify from 'fastify';
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page
import { theAuthFastify } from '@glinr/theauth-fastify';

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});

const app = Fastify({ logger: true });

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

await app.register(theAuthFastify(theauth, { mcp, authenticate }), {
  prefix: '/api/theauth',
});

app.get('/health', async () => ({ ok: true }));

await app.listen({ port: 3000, host: '0.0.0.0' });
```

# NestJS

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/nestjs

`TheAuthModule.forRoot(options)` is a NestJS dynamic module that mounts all theAuth routes as Express middleware. Import it once in your root `AppModule`.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-nestjs
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

```typescript
// lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store.js'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Import TheAuthModule">

```typescript
// app.module.ts
import { Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { TheAuthModule } from '@glinr/theauth-nestjs';
import { theauth, mcp } from './lib/theauth.js';

@Module({
  imports: [
    TheAuthModule.forRoot({
      theauth,
      mcp,
      authenticate, // who may call /agents, /delegations, /audit, /dashboard
      basePath: '/api/theauth', // default
    }),
  ],
})
export class AppModule {}
```

</Step>
<Step title="Bootstrap">

```typescript
// main.ts
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { AppModule } from './app.module.js';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
  await app.listen(3000);
}

bootstrap();
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  NestJS uses Express under the hood by default. The adapter mounts an Express Router directly, so no extra configuration is needed.
</Info>

## Route prefix

The default mount path is `/api/theauth`. Change it with the `basePath` option:

```typescript
TheAuthModule.forRoot({ theauth, basePath: '/auth' })
```

All theAuth routes will then be available under `/auth/*`.

## Without a module

If you prefer to mount routes imperatively in `main.ts` rather than importing a module, use `theAuthMiddleware` directly:

```typescript
// main.ts
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { AppModule } from './app.module.js';
import { theAuthMiddleware } from '@glinr/theauth-nestjs';
import { theauth, mcp } from './lib/theauth.js';

async function bootstrap() {
  const app = await NestFactory.create(AppModule);
// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

  app.use('/api/theauth', theAuthMiddleware({ theauth, mcp, authenticate }));
  await app.listen(3000);
}

bootstrap();
```

## MCP endpoints

Pass `mcp` to enable the MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server:

```typescript
TheAuthModule.forRoot({ theauth, mcp, basePath: '/api/theauth' })
// registers:
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
// GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
// GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
// POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
```

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts

```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

Every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. See the [route reference](/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route for agents

```typescript
import { Controller, Get, Req, UseGuards } from '@nestjs/common';
import { getAgent, requireScope } from '@glinr/theauth-nestjs';

@Controller('invoices')
export class InvoicesController {
  @Get()
  @UseGuards(requireScope(theauth, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' }))
  list(@Req() req: { agent?: { id: string } }) {
    return { agentId: getAgent(req)?.id };
  }
}
```

Missing or invalid bearer token returns 401 and a denied scope returns 403. The body is `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, where `code` is the decision code (for example `no_permission`). See the [requireScope guide](/require-scope).

# Next.js

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/nextjs

`theAuthNextjs(theauth, options?)` returns named route handlers `{ GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS }` for the Next.js App Router. Mount them in a catch-all route file so all theAuth paths are handled.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-nextjs
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

Create this in a shared module so it is initialized once at server startup:

```typescript
// lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Create the catch-all route">

Create `app/api/theauth/[...theauth]/route.ts`. The `[...theauth]` segment catches every sub-path under `/api/theauth/`.

```typescript
// app/api/theauth/[...theauth]/route.ts
import { theAuthNextjs } from '@glinr/theauth-nextjs';
import { theauth, mcp } from '@/lib/theauth';

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

const handlers = theAuthNextjs(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });

export const GET = handlers.GET;
export const POST = handlers.POST;
export const PATCH = handlers.PATCH;
export const DELETE = handlers.DELETE;
export const OPTIONS = handlers.OPTIONS;
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  The `basePath` option defaults to `/api/theauth`. If you mount at a different path such as `/api/auth/theauth`, pass `basePath: '/api/auth/theauth'` so the handler can strip the prefix correctly.
</Info>

## Options

```typescript
interface AuthNextjsOptions {
  mcp?: McpAuthModule;     // enables MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints
  basePath?: string;       // defaults to '/api/theauth'
}
```

## MCP endpoints

When `mcp` is passed, the following endpoints are available:

```
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
```

```ts

```

## Endpoint reference

Every adapter serves the same routes with the same status codes. See the [route reference](/adapters/routes).


  </Card>

# Nuxt

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/nuxt

`theAuthNuxt(theauth, options?)` returns an H3 `EventHandler`. Mount it in a catch-all server route so all theAuth paths are handled.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-nuxt
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

Create this outside the event handler so it is initialized once at server startup:

```typescript
// server/utils/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Create the catch-all route">

In Nuxt, a file named `[...].ts` in the server routes directory catches all sub-paths. Create `server/api/theauth/[...].ts`:

```typescript
// server/api/theauth/[...].ts
import { theAuthNuxt } from '@glinr/theauth-nuxt';
import { theauth, mcp } from '../utils/theauth';

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

export default theAuthNuxt(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  The `basePath` option defaults to `/api/theauth`. If your Nuxt app uses a different route prefix, pass `basePath` to match.
</Info>

## Options

`theAuthNuxt(theauth, options?)` takes the same options as the core handler (`createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http`), so they are identical on every adapter:

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `mcp` | `McpAuthModule` | Enables the MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints |
| `basePath` | `string` | URL prefix before the catch-all segment. Defaults to `/api/theauth` |
| `routes` | `{ management?, mcp?, plugins?, explain? }` | Turn route groups off. `mcp` also takes `{ register, authorize, token, revoke, jwks }` booleans |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | Largest request body, default 1 MiB (413 above it) |
| `authenticate`, `allowUnauthenticated`, `trustedProxy`, `rateLimit`, `trustedOrigins`, `csrf` | | Shared security options |

Every route and status code is listed on the [route reference](https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route with `requireScope`

```typescript
import { requireScope } from '@glinr/theauth-nuxt';

// server/api/invoices.get.ts
export default requireScope(theauth, { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' }, (event) => ({
  agent: event.context.agent.id,
}));
```

`requireScope(theauth, { action, resource }, handler)` reads the agent bearer token and checks it may perform the action. It answers 401 (`invalid_token`, `agent_not_found`, `agent_revoked`, `agent_expired`) or 403 (any other denial) with body `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, and otherwise passes the agent (without its token) on via `event.context.agent`. Pass `clientIp` to feed `ipAllowlist` constraints.

## MCP endpoints

When `mcp` is passed, the MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server is available at:

```
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
POST /api/theauth/mcp/revoke
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/jwks
```

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
export default theAuthNuxt(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } });
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

See the [route reference](/adapters/routes) for every route, its auth level and status codes.

## Full example

```typescript
// server/api/theauth/[...].ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page
import { theAuthNuxt } from '@glinr/theauth-nuxt';

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

export default theAuthNuxt(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });
```

All theAuth routes are then available at `/api/theauth/...` within your Nuxt server.

# SvelteKit

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/sveltekit

`theAuthSvelteKit(theauth, options?)` returns named route handlers `{ GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS }`. Mount them in a catch-all server route file so all theAuth paths are handled.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-sveltekit
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

```typescript
// src/lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Create the catch-all route">

Create `src/routes/api/theauth/[...path]/+server.ts`. The `[...path]` segment catches every sub-path under `/api/theauth/`.

```typescript
// src/routes/api/theauth/[...path]/+server.ts
import { theAuthSvelteKit } from '@glinr/theauth-sveltekit';
import { theauth, mcp } from '$lib/theauth';

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

const handlers = theAuthSvelteKit(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });

export const GET = handlers.GET;
export const POST = handlers.POST;
export const PATCH = handlers.PATCH;
export const DELETE = handlers.DELETE;
export const OPTIONS = handlers.OPTIONS;
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Info>
  SvelteKit passes a standard Web API `Request` to route handlers, so the adapter delegates directly to the theAuth dispatcher without any conversion.
</Info>

## Options

`theAuthSvelteKit(theauth, options?)` takes the same options as the core handler (`createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http`), so they are identical on every adapter:

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `mcp` | `McpAuthModule` | Enables the MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints |
| `basePath` | `string` | URL prefix before the catch-all segment. Defaults to `/api/theauth` |
| `routes` | `{ management?, mcp?, plugins?, explain? }` | Turn route groups off. `mcp` also takes `{ register, authorize, token, revoke, jwks }` booleans |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | Largest request body, default 1 MiB (413 above it) |
| `authenticate`, `allowUnauthenticated`, `trustedProxy`, `rateLimit`, `trustedOrigins`, `csrf` | | Shared security options |

Every route and status code is listed on the [route reference](https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route with `requireScope`

```typescript

  theauth,
  { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' },
  ({ locals }) => Response.json({ agent: locals.agent.id }),
);
```

```
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
POST /api/theauth/mcp/revoke
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/jwks
```

## Endpoint reference

```
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
POST /api/theauth/mcp/revoke
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/jwks
```

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
const handlers = theAuthTanStack(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } });
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

See the [route reference](/adapters/routes) for every route, its auth level and status codes.

## Full example

```typescript
// app/routes/api/theauth.$.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page
import { theAuthTanStack } from '@glinr/theauth-tanstack';

const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: process.env.DATABASE_URL! },
  baseUrl: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!,
    baseUrl: `${process.env.AUTH_BASE_URL!}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

const handlers = theAuthTanStack(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });

export const GET = handlers.GET;
export const POST = handlers.POST;
export const PATCH = handlers.PATCH;
export const DELETE = handlers.DELETE;
export const OPTIONS = handlers.OPTIONS;
```

# Astro

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/astro

`theAuthAstro(theauth, options?)` returns named route handlers `{ GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, ALL }`. Mount them in a catch-all API page so all theAuth paths are handled. Use individual named exports or the `ALL` catch-all handler.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth @glinr/theauth-astro
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step title="Create the theauth instance">

```typescript
// src/lib/theauth.ts
import { createTheAuth } from '@glinr/theauth';
import { createMcpModule } from '@glinr/theauth/mcp';
import { mcpStore } from './mcp-store'; // storage callbacks, see the MCP page

export const theauth = await createTheAuth({
  database: { provider: 'postgres', url: import.meta.env.DATABASE_URL },
  baseUrl: import.meta.env.AUTH_BASE_URL,
  mcp: { enabled: true }, // creates the MCP tables
});

// baseUrl is the public origin plus the adapter mount path (default /api/theauth)
export const mcp = createMcpModule({
  config: {
    enabled: true,
    issuer: import.meta.env.AUTH_BASE_URL,
    baseUrl: `${import.meta.env.AUTH_BASE_URL}/api/theauth`,
    signingSecret: process.env.MCP_SIGNING_SECRET!, // at least 32 characters
  },
  ...mcpStore,
});
```

</Step>
<Step title="Create the catch-all route">

Create `src/pages/api/theauth/[...path].ts`. The `[...path]` spread catches every sub-path under `/api/theauth/`.

```typescript
// src/pages/api/theauth/[...path].ts
import { theAuthAstro } from '@glinr/theauth-astro';
import { theauth, mcp } from '@/lib/theauth';

// Who may call the management routes. Return { id } to allow, null to reject (401).
// resolveUser needs an auth.adapter; with only auth.session, omit authenticate
// and any valid session is accepted.
const authenticate = async (request: Request) => {
  const user = await theauth.auth.resolveUser(request);
  return user ? { id: user.id } : null;
};

const handlers = theAuthAstro(theauth, { mcp, authenticate });

export const GET = handlers.GET;
export const POST = handlers.POST;
export const PATCH = handlers.PATCH;
export const DELETE = handlers.DELETE;
export const OPTIONS = handlers.OPTIONS;
```

Or use the `ALL` handler to catch every HTTP method in one export:

```typescript
export const ALL = handlers.ALL;
```

</Step>
</Steps>

<Warning>
  Astro requires `output: 'server'` or `output: 'hybrid'` in `astro.config.mjs` to enable API routes. Static output mode does not support server-side route handlers.
</Warning>

## Options

`theAuthAstro(theauth, options?)` takes the same options as the core handler (`createTheAuthHandler` from `@glinr/theauth/http`), so they are identical on every adapter:

| Option | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `mcp` | `McpAuthModule` | Enables the MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints |
| `basePath` | `string` | URL prefix before the catch-all segment. Defaults to `/api/theauth` |
| `routes` | `{ management?, mcp?, plugins?, explain? }` | Turn route groups off. `mcp` also takes `{ register, authorize, token, revoke, jwks }` booleans |
| `maxBodyBytes` | `number` | Largest request body, default 1 MiB (413 above it) |
| `authenticate`, `allowUnauthenticated`, `trustedProxy`, `rateLimit`, `trustedOrigins`, `csrf` | | Shared security options |

Every route and status code is listed on the [route reference](https://docs.theauth.dev/adapters/routes).

## Protect a route with `requireScope`

```typescript
import { requireScope } from '@glinr/theauth-astro';

export const GET = requireScope(
  theauth,
  { action: 'read', resource: 'invoices' },
  ({ locals }) => Response.json({ agent: locals.agent.id }),
);
```

`requireScope(theauth, { action, resource }, handler)` reads the agent bearer token and checks it may perform the action. It answers 401 (`invalid_token`, `agent_not_found`, `agent_revoked`, `agent_expired`) or 403 (any other denial) with body `{ "error": { "code", "message" } }`, and otherwise passes the agent (without its token) on via `locals.agent`. Pass `clientIp` to feed `ipAllowlist` constraints.

## MCP endpoints

When `mcp` is passed, the MCP OAuth 2.1 endpoints are available at:

```
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
GET  /api/theauth/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource
POST /api/theauth/mcp/register
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/authorize
POST /api/theauth/mcp/token
POST /api/theauth/mcp/revoke
GET  /api/theauth/mcp/jwks
```

## Management routes and client IP

With the default session guard, a signed-in user only acts on their own agents, delegations and audit rows. A custom `authenticate` resolver is a trust decision and sees everything.

The adapter does not read forwarded headers for the client IP. Behind a proxy, set `trustedProxy` with `trustedProxyCount` or `trustedHeader`, or `ipAllowlist` constraints cannot match.

```ts
const handlers = theAuthAstro(theauth, { authenticate, trustedProxy: { trustedProxyCount: 1 } });
```

On Cloudflare use `trustedHeader: 'cf-connecting-ip'`. Only trust a header your edge overwrites.

## Endpoint reference

See the [route reference](/adapters/routes) for every route, its auth level and status codes.

# TypeScript client

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/client-sdk

## Overview

`@glinr/theauth-client` is a typed HTTP client for the theAuth REST API. It covers agents, authorization, delegations, audit logs, and MCP server registration.

<Info>
  Zero dependencies. No Node.js builtins. Works in browser, Node.js, Deno, and Bun, anywhere the Fetch API is available.
</Info>

<Warning>
  The client and the adapters in this repository do not fully line up yet. The adapters wrap every success body as `{ "data": ... }` and the client returns the parsed body as is, without unwrapping it. The adapters answer a denied authorization with HTTP `403`, which the client throws as a `TheAuthApiError` instead of returning `allowed: false`. And four client calls target paths the adapters do not serve: `authorize` (`POST /agents/:id/authorize`), `authorizeByToken` (`POST /authorize` with a bearer header; the adapters take `agentId` there and use `POST /authorize/token` for tokens), `delegations.getEffectivePermissions` (`GET /delegations/:agentId/permissions`), and all of `mcp.*` (`/mcp/servers`). The examples below show the API the client is typed for. Check it against your server before relying on it, or call the [REST endpoints](/api) directly.
</Warning>

## Installation

```bash
npm install @glinr/theauth-client
```

## Creating a client

```typescript
import { createTheAuthClient } from '@glinr/theauth-client';

const client = createTheAuthClient({
  baseUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/api/theauth',
  token: process.env.THEAUTH_API_TOKEN,
});
```

<ParamField path="baseUrl" type="string">Base URL for the theAuth API, without a trailing slash.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="token" type="string" default="undefined">Bearer token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request. The adapters protect `/agents`, `/delegations`, `/audit` and `POST /authorize`, so this must be a credential your adapter's `authenticate` function accepts (a theAuth session token when you rely on `auth.session`). An agent token is not accepted there. See [Adapters](/adapters#authenticate-the-management-routes).</ParamField>
<ParamField path="headers" type={`Record<string, string>`} default="{}">Extra headers merged into every request. Useful for API gateways that require custom headers.</ParamField>

## Agents

```typescript
// Create
const agent = await client.agents.create({
  ownerId: 'user-123',
  name: 'data-pipeline-bot',
  type: 'autonomous',
  permissions: [
    { resource: 'db:reports:*', actions: ['read'] },
  ],
});

console.log(agent.token); // ta_..., save this now

// List with optional filters
const active = await client.agents.list({
  userId: 'user-123',
  status: 'active',
  type: 'autonomous',
});

// Get by ID (returns null for 404)
const found = await client.agents.get('agt_abc123');

// Update name and permissions (a new permissions array replaces the old one)
const updated = await client.agents.update('agt_abc123', {
  name: 'data-pipeline-bot-v2',
  permissions: [
    { resource: 'db:reports:*', actions: ['read', 'export'] },
  ],
});

// Rotate the token
const rotated = await client.agents.rotate('agt_abc123');
console.log(rotated.token); // new token, old one is now invalid

// Revoke
await client.agents.revoke('agt_abc123');
```

## Authorization

Two paths: by agent ID (when you manage the agent directly) or by raw bearer token (when the token comes in from an HTTP request).

```typescript
// By agent ID, useful in admin or backend code
const byId = await client.authorize('agt_abc123', {
  action: 'read',
  resource: 'db:reports:monthly',
  arguments: { reportId: 'r-456' },
});

if (!byId.allowed) {
  console.error(byId.reason); // free-text explanation of the denial
}

// By bearer token, useful in middleware
const bearerToken = request.headers.get('Authorization')?.replace('Bearer ', '') ?? '';
const byToken = await client.authorizeByToken(bearerToken, {
  action: 'read',
  resource: 'db:reports:monthly',
});
```

## Delegations

```typescript
// Delegate from one agent to another with a subset of permissions
const chain = await client.delegations.create({
  fromAgent: 'agt_parent',
  toAgent: 'agt_child',
  permissions: [
    { resource: 'db:reports:*', actions: ['read'] },
  ],
  expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString(), // 1 hour
});

// List delegations where the agent is the source (fromAgent)
const delegations = await client.delegations.list('agt_parent');

// Effective permissions: the permissions the agent currently holds through
// active, unexpired delegations (its own permissions are not included)
const effective = await client.delegations.getEffectivePermissions('agt_child');

// Revoke a delegation
await client.delegations.revoke(chain.id);
```

## Audit log

```typescript
// Query with filters
const entries = await client.audit.query({
  agentId: 'agt_abc123',
  since: '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z',
  until: '2024-02-01T00:00:00Z',
  result: 'denied',
  limit: 100,
  offset: 0,
});

// Export as CSV for billing or compliance (returns the file contents as a string)
const csv = await client.audit.export({
  format: 'csv',
  since: '2024-01-01T00:00:00Z',
  until: '2024-02-01T00:00:00Z',
});

// Export as JSON
const json = await client.audit.export({ format: 'json' });
```

## Error handling

All methods throw `TheAuthApiError` when the server returns a non-2xx response or the network call fails.

```typescript
import { TheAuthApiError } from '@glinr/theauth-client';

try {
  const agent = await client.agents.rotate('agt_nonexistent');
} catch (err) {
  if (err instanceof TheAuthApiError) {
    console.error(err.code);    // e.g. 'NOT_FOUND', 'BAD_REQUEST', 'INTERNAL_ERROR'
    console.error(err.message); // human-readable message
    console.error(err.status);  // HTTP status code
  }
}
```

`TheAuthApiError` also covers network errors: if `fetch` itself throws, you get `code: 'NETWORK_ERROR'` and `status: 0`.

<Warning>
  `client.agents.get` and `client.mcp.get` return `null` for 404 rather than throwing. All other methods throw `TheAuthApiError` on any error response.
</Warning>

## MCP servers

These calls hit `/mcp/servers`, which the bundled adapters do not serve (see the warning above). In your own server code, use the in-process registry `theauth.mcp.register`, `list`, and `get` instead.

```typescript
// Register an MCP server
const server = await client.mcp.register({
  name: 'github-mcp',
  endpoint: 'https://mcp.yourapp.com/github',
  tools: ['list_repos', 'get_issue', 'create_comment'],
  authRequired: true,
  rateLimit: { rpm: 60 },
});

// List all registered servers
const servers = await client.mcp.list();

// Get one by ID (returns null for 404)
const found = await client.mcp.get(server.id);
```

## Session refetch and SSR

`createSessionStore` keeps a session in step with the server. It is the same store the React, Vue, Svelte and Solid bindings use.

```typescript
import { createSessionStore } from "@glinr/theauth-client";

const store = createSessionStore({
  basePath: "/api/theauth",
  storage: typeof localStorage === "undefined" ? undefined : localStorage,
  refetch: { intervalMs: 5 * 60_000 },
});
```

| Trigger | Option | Default |
|-|-|-|
| Window focus, or the tab becoming visible | `refetch.onFocus` | on |
| Browser back online | `refetch.onReconnect` | on |
| Fixed interval | `refetch.intervalMs` | off (0) |
| Interval while offline | `refetch.whenOffline` | off |

The triggers run while the store has at least one subscriber and stop when the last one leaves. `store.startAutoRefresh(options)` starts them by hand and returns a `stop` function, `store.destroy()` stops them and aborts a refresh in flight. With no `window` (a server, a worker, an edge runtime) every trigger is a no-op, so the same code runs there. `refetch.env` takes your own `window`, `document` and `isOnline`, which is how the tests drive it with fake event targets.

`store.refresh()` calls `GET {basePath}/auth/session`. Concurrent calls, such as focus and visibility firing together, share one request. A 401 or 403 clears the session. A network error or a 5xx keeps what the store has, so a dropped connection does not sign anyone out. A sign out that happens while a refresh is running wins over the refresh result.

For SSR, resolve the session on the server and seed the store so the first render matches and no request is needed:

```typescript
store.hydrateSession({ user: { id: "u_123", email: "ada@example.com" }, expiresAt });
```

Leave `token` out of the HTML you render. Cookie sessions do not need it, and the store asks the server again on the next refresh. An expired or malformed value counts as signed out, and `hydrateSession(null)` means the server found no session. Neither the store nor the refetch code logs anything, and no error message contains a token.

The routes the store calls are `POST /auth/username/sign-in`, `POST /auth/username/sign-up`, `POST /auth/sign-out` and `GET /auth/session`. The core has no email and password route, so set `signInPath`, `signUpPath` and `identifierField` if you serve your own.
