# React hooks

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/react

## Overview

`@glinr/theauth-react` provides React hooks and a context provider for building auth UIs on top of theAuth. It works with Next.js App Router, Next.js Pages Router, Vite, and any React 18+ setup (the package declares React 18 or later as a peer dependency).

The package itself has no Node.js dependencies, it runs entirely in the browser. Your theAuth API handler can sit behind Next.js Edge Runtime, Cloudflare Workers, Deno Deploy, or any other edge runtime, and the hooks talk to it over standard `fetch`.

<Info>
  All hooks must be rendered inside `TheAuthProvider`. The provider talks to your theAuth API route, no direct database access from the browser.
</Info>

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-react
```

## Provider setup

Wrap your app with `TheAuthProvider`. In Next.js App Router, create a client component and import it from your root layout.

```tsx
// app/providers.tsx
'use client';
import { TheAuthProvider } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

export function Providers({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <TheAuthProvider basePath="/api/theauth">
      {children}
    </TheAuthProvider>
  );
}
```

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx
import { Providers } from './providers';

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <Providers>{children}</Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

<ParamField path="basePath" type="string" default="&quot;/api/theauth&quot;">Path to your theAuth API handler. Must match the route you mounted in the adapter.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="external" type="ExternalAuthConfig" default="undefined">Delegate authentication to an external API instead of the managed mode described below. See "External auth mode".</ParamField>
<ParamField path="managed" type="ManagedAuthConfig" default="undefined">Options for managed mode: `refetch` (focus, reconnect, interval), `initialSession` (SSR seed), `signInPath`, `signUpPath` and `identifierField`. See [Session refetch and SSR](/client-sdk#session-refetch-and-ssr).</ParamField>
<ParamField path="debug" type="boolean" default="false">Enable verbose auth state logging (also enabled when `localStorage.DEBUG === "theauth"`).</ParamField>

<Info>
In managed mode (no `external` prop) the session token is stored in `localStorage` under the key `theauth_session`. On load the provider shows that stored session at once, then confirms it with `GET {basePath}/auth/session`. A 401 or 403 clears it. A network error or a 5xx keeps it, so going offline never signs anyone out. Cookie-only sessions work too: with nothing stored, the same request picks up the session cookie.
</Info>

<Warning>
Managed mode signs in and up through the username module: `POST {basePath}/auth/username/sign-in` and `POST {basePath}/auth/username/sign-up` with `{ username, password }` (plus `name` for sign-up), answering `{ user, session: { token, expiresAt } }`. The first argument of `signIn` and `signUp` is sent as `username`. theAuth core has no email-and-password route, so for one of your own set `managed.signInPath`, `managed.signUpPath` and `managed.identifierField` (for example `"email"`), and return the same response shape.
</Warning>

## useSession

Returns the raw session object. Useful when you need the session token or expiry directly.

```tsx
import { useSession } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

function SessionDebug() {
  const { session, isLoading } = useSession();

  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading...</p>;
  if (!session) return <p>No active session.</p>;

  return (
    <p>
      Session expires: {session.expiresAt ? new Date(session.expiresAt).toLocaleString() : 'unknown'}
    </p>
  );
}
```

<ParamField path="session" type="TheAuthSession | null">The current session (`{ token, user, expiresAt? }`). Null when unauthenticated or still loading.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="isLoading" type="boolean">True during the initial session restore.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="refresh" type={`() => Promise<void>`}>Re-read the session from the server. In managed mode this calls `GET {basePath}/auth/session`, in external mode it re-fetches the current user. Concurrent calls share one request.</ParamField>

## useUser

Returns the authenticated user and a boolean flag. This is the most common hook for protecting UI.

```tsx
import { useUser } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

function ProfileCard() {
  const { user, isAuthenticated, isLoading } = useUser();

  if (isLoading) return <Skeleton />;
  if (!isAuthenticated || !user) return <SignInPrompt />;

  return (
    <div>
      <p>{user.name}</p>
      <p>{user.email}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

<ParamField path="user" type="TheAuthUser | null">The authenticated user (`{ id, email?, name?, image? }`). Null when unauthenticated.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="isAuthenticated" type="boolean">True when a valid session with a user is present.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="isLoading" type="boolean">True during the initial load. Avoid rendering auth-gated UI until this is false.</ParamField>

## useSignIn

Handles email and password sign-in. Returns `signIn(email, password)` plus `isLoading` and `error` (a string or `null`).

The hook posts to `POST {basePath}/auth/username/sign-in` by default (see the warning above about the server route).

```tsx
import { useSignIn } from '@glinr/theauth-react';
import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation';

function SignInForm() {
  const { signIn, isLoading, error } = useSignIn();
  const router = useRouter();

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    const form = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    const result = await signIn(
      form.get('email') as string,
      form.get('password') as string,
    );
    if (result.success) router.push('/dashboard');
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <input name="email" type="email" />
      <input name="password" type="password" />
      {error && <p>{error}</p>}
      <button type="submit" disabled={isLoading}>
        {isLoading ? 'Signing in...' : 'Sign in'}
      </button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## useSignUp

Handles new account registration with `signUp(email, password, name?)`. Posts to `POST {basePath}/auth/username/sign-up` by default.

```tsx
import { useSignUp } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

function SignUpForm() {
  const { signUp, isLoading, error } = useSignUp();

  async function handleSubmit(e: React.FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
    e.preventDefault();
    const form = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
    await signUp(
      form.get('email') as string,
      form.get('password') as string,
      form.get('name') as string,
    );
  }

  return (
    <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
      <input name="name" type="text" />
      <input name="email" type="email" />
      <input name="password" type="password" />
      {error && <p>{error}</p>}
      <button type="submit" disabled={isLoading}>Create account</button>
    </form>
  );
}
```

## useSignOut

Signs the user out. `signOut()` takes no arguments. In managed mode it clears React state and `localStorage` first, then calls `POST {basePath}/auth/sign-out` to revoke the session on the server (the stored token goes as a bearer header, the cookie is sent too). In external mode it calls your logout path. It does not redirect, navigate yourself afterwards.

```tsx
import { useSignOut } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

function NavBar() {
  const { signOut } = useSignOut();

  return (
    <nav>
      <button onClick={async () => { await signOut(); window.location.assign('/login'); }}>
        Sign out
      </button>
    </nav>
  );
}
```

## useAgents

Lets your UI list, create, revoke, and rotate agents through your theAuth API. `useAgents(basePath = '/api/theauth')` takes its own base path and reads the user from the provider.

```tsx
import { useAgents, useUser } from '@glinr/theauth-react';

function Dashboard() {
  const { user, isAuthenticated } = useUser();
  const { agents, create, revoke, isLoading: agentsLoading } = useAgents();

  if (!isAuthenticated || !user) return null;

  async function handleCreate() {
    await create({
      ownerId: user.id,
      name: 'my-bot',
      type: 'autonomous',
      permissions: [
        { resource: 'reports:*', actions: ['read'] },
      ],
    });
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={handleCreate}>New agent</button>
      {agentsLoading && <p>Loading agents...</p>}
      {agents.map((agent) => (
        <div key={agent.id}>
          <span>{agent.name}</span>
          <button onClick={() => revoke(agent.id)}>Revoke</button>
        </div>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

The hook calls `GET {basePath}/agents?userId=<id>` (expecting `{ data: Agent[] }`), `POST {basePath}/agents`, `DELETE {basePath}/agents/:id`, and `POST {basePath}/agents/:id/rotate`, all with `credentials: 'include'`. Single-agent responses are expected as `{ data: Agent }`.

<ParamField path="agents" type="TheAuthAgent[]">Current list of agents for the authenticated user.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="create" type={`(input: CreateAgentInput) => Promise<ActionResult<TheAuthAgent>>`}>Create a new agent. `CreateAgentInput` requires `ownerId`, `name`, `type`, and `permissions`. The list reloads on success.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="revoke" type={`(agentId: string) => Promise<ActionResult>`}>Revoke an agent by ID. The list reloads on success.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="rotate" type={`(agentId: string) => Promise<ActionResult<TheAuthAgent>>`}>Rotate an agent's token. The returned agent carries the new token.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="load" type={`() => Promise<void>`}>Re-fetch the agent list manually.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="isLoading" type="boolean">True while the agent list is loading.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="error" type="string | null">The last load error message.</ParamField>

`ActionResult<T>` is `{ success: true, data: T } | { success: false, error: string }`.

## External auth mode

Pass `external` to delegate authentication to an API you already run, for example one that manages httpOnly cookies. The provider then fetches the user from `apiUrl + mePath` (default `/api/auth/me`), sends login redirects to `loginPath` (default `/auth/github`), and calls `logoutPath` (default `/auth/logout`, method `POST`) on sign out. No session is stored in `localStorage`. `external.refetch` and `external.initialUser` work the same way as in managed mode, and a network error during a refetch keeps the current user.

```tsx
<TheAuthProvider
  external={{
    apiUrl: 'https://api.example.com',
    mePath: '/api/auth/me',
    loginPath: '/auth/github',
    logoutPath: '/auth/logout',
    refreshPath: '/auth/refresh', // enables rotation, see useRotateSession
  }}
>
  {children}
</TheAuthProvider>
```

`useRotateSession()` returns `{ rotate, status, isOnline }` for the token rotation flow. It only does work when `refreshPath` is set, otherwise `rotate()` resolves with `{ success: false, code: 'network_error' }`.

# Vue

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/vue

`@glinr/theauth-vue` provides Vue 3 composables and an app plugin for building auth UIs. It works with Vite, Nuxt, and any Vue 3 setup.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-vue
```

## Setup

Register the plugin in your Vue app:

```typescript title="main.ts"
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { createTheAuthPlugin } from '@glinr/theauth-vue'; // [!code highlight]
import App from './App.vue';

const app = createApp(App);

app.use(createTheAuthPlugin({ // [!code highlight]
  basePath: '/api/theauth', // [!code highlight]
})); // [!code highlight]

app.mount('#app');
```

### Nuxt setup

In Nuxt, create a plugin file:

```typescript title="plugins/theauth.client.ts"
import { createTheAuthPlugin } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxtApp) => {
  nuxtApp.vueApp.use(createTheAuthPlugin({
    basePath: '/api/theauth',
  }));
});
```

## useSession

Returns the current session state. Reactive, updates when the user signs in or out.

```vue title="components/NavBar.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useSession } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { session, isLoading } = useSession();
</script>

<template>
  <nav>
    <span v-if="isLoading">Loading...</span>
    <span v-else-if="session">{{ session.user.name }}</span>
    <a v-else href="/sign-in">Sign in</a>
  </nav>
</template>
```

## useUser

Returns the current user object, or `null` if signed out.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useUser } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { user } = useUser();
</script>
```

## useSignIn / useSignUp / useSignOut

```vue title="pages/sign-in.vue"
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useSignIn } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { signIn, isLoading, error } = useSignIn();

async function handleSubmit(email: string, password: string) {
  await signIn({ email, password });
  // Redirect on success. The composable does not navigate automatically.
}
</script>
```

```typescript title="Sign up"
import { useSignUp } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { signUp, isLoading, error } = useSignUp();
await signUp({ email, password, name });
```

```typescript title="Sign out"
import { useSignOut } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { signOut } = useSignOut();
await signOut();
```

## useAgents

Lists and manages agent identities for the current user.

```typescript
import { useAgents } from '@glinr/theauth-vue';

const { agents, createAgent, revokeAgent, isLoading } = useAgents();

// Create a new agent
await createAgent({ name: 'My AI assistant', permissions: ['read:data'] });
```

## Plugin configuration reference

<ParamField path="basePath" type="string" default="'/api/theauth'">Base path where your theAuth handler is mounted.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="refetch" type="RefetchOptions">Refetch the session on window focus, reconnect or an interval. Off unless set. See [Session refetch and SSR](/client-sdk#session-refetch-and-ssr).</ParamField>
<ParamField path="initialSession" type="HydrateInput | null">Session the server already resolved. Skips the first request.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signInPath" type="string" default="'/auth/username/sign-in'">Route for `signIn`. Core has no email and password route, so point this at your own if you need one.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signUpPath" type="string" default="'/auth/username/sign-up'">Route for `signUp`.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="identifierField" type="string" default="'username'">Body field that carries the first argument of `signIn` and `signUp`.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="storage" type="SessionStorageLike">Defaults to `window.localStorage` when the browser allows it.</ParamField>

On install the plugin shows a stored session at once, then confirms it with `GET {basePath}/auth/session`. `signOut` clears local state first, then calls `POST {basePath}/auth/sign-out` to revoke the session on the server.

```typescript
app.use(
  createTheAuthPlugin({
    basePath: "/api/theauth",
    refetch: { intervalMs: 5 * 60_000 },
  }),
);
```

# Svelte

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/svelte

`@glinr/theauth-svelte` provides reactive Svelte stores for sessions and agents. It works with Svelte 4+, SvelteKit, and plain Vite setups.

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-svelte
```

## Setup

Create a client instance once and export its stores from a shared module:

```typescript title="src/lib/theauth.ts"
import { createTheAuthClient } from '@glinr/theauth-svelte';

export const { session, user, isAuthenticated, isLoading, signIn, signUp, signOut, refresh } =
  createTheAuthClient({ basePath: '/api/theauth' });
```

The client fetches the session from your theAuth handler in the browser. There is no SvelteKit hooks helper in this package, so `locals.session` is not populated for you. To mount the server routes, use the [SvelteKit adapter](/adapters/sveltekit) (`@glinr/theauth-sveltekit`).

## Session store

`session` holds the session object or `null`. `user` and `isAuthenticated` are derived from it, and `isLoading` is true until the first fetch settles.

```svelte title="src/routes/+page.svelte"
<script lang="ts">
  import { session, user, isLoading } from '$lib/theauth';
</script>

{#if $isLoading}
  <p>Loading...</p>
{:else if $session}
  <p>Signed in as {$user?.email}</p>
{:else}
  <a href="/sign-in">Sign in</a>
{/if}
```

## Sign in, sign up, sign out

`signIn` and `signUp` take positional arguments and resolve to `{ success: true, data }` or `{ success: false, error }`, where `error` is a string.

```svelte title="src/routes/sign-in/+page.svelte"
<script lang="ts">
  import { signIn } from '$lib/theauth';

  let email = '';
  let password = '';
  let error = '';

  async function handleSubmit() {
    const result = await signIn(email, password);
    if (!result.success) {
      error = result.error;
    }
  }
</script>
```

```typescript title="Sign up and sign out"
import { signUp, signOut } from '$lib/theauth';

await signUp(email, password, name);
await signOut();
```

## createAgentStore

Manage agent identities in reactive Svelte stores. Pass the `user` store from your client and the agent list loads when a user is present, or call `load(userId)` yourself.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { createAgentStore } from '@glinr/theauth-svelte';
  import { user } from '$lib/theauth';

  const { agents, create, revoke, isLoading, error } = createAgentStore({
    basePath: '/api/theauth',
    user,
  });

  async function addAgent() {
    if (!$user) return;
    await create({
      ownerId: $user.id,
      name: 'My assistant',
      type: 'delegated',
      permissions: [{ resource: 'data', actions: ['read'] }],
    });
  }
</script>

{#each $agents as agent}
  <div>{agent.name} <button on:click={() => revoke(agent.id)}>Revoke</button></div>
{/each}
```

The store also exposes `rotate(agentId)`.

## Client configuration reference

<ParamField path="basePath" type="string" default="'/api/theauth'">Base path where your theAuth handler is mounted.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="refetch" type="RefetchOptions">Refetch the session on window focus, reconnect or an interval. Runs while any of the client's stores has a subscriber. See [Session refetch and SSR](/client-sdk#session-refetch-and-ssr).</ParamField>
<ParamField path="initialSession" type="HydrateInput | null">Session the server already resolved. Skips the first request. Also available later as `client.hydrateSession(initial)`.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signInPath" type="string" default="'/auth/username/sign-in'">Route for `signIn`. Core has no email and password route, so point this at your own if you need one.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signUpPath" type="string" default="'/auth/username/sign-up'">Route for `signUp`.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="identifierField" type="string" default="'username'">Body field that carries the first argument of `signIn` and `signUp`.</ParamField>

On creation the client shows a stored session at once, then confirms it with `GET {basePath}/auth/session`. `signOut` clears local state first, then calls `POST {basePath}/auth/sign-out`. `client.destroy()` stops the refetch triggers and aborts an in-flight refresh.

# Solid

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/solid

`@glinr/theauth-client` ships `createSessionStore` (plain state, subscribe, sign in and out) and `createSolidAuth`, which turns the store into Solid accessors. Pass in the two Solid primitives you already import. The client takes no dependency on `solid-js`, so it works with any 1.x release.

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-client solid-js
```

```typescript
// lib/auth.ts
import { createSignal, onCleanup } from "solid-js";
import { createSessionStore, createSolidAuth } from "@glinr/theauth-client";

const store = createSessionStore({
  basePath: "/api/theauth",
  storage: typeof localStorage === "undefined" ? undefined : localStorage,
});

export const { useSession, useUser, useIsAuthenticated } = createSolidAuth(
  { createSignal, onCleanup },
  store,
);
export { store };
```

```tsx
// components/Profile.tsx
import { store, useUser } from "../lib/auth";

export function Profile() {
  const user = useUser();
  return (
    <button onClick={() => store.signOut()}>
      {user()?.email ?? "Sign in"}
    </button>
  );
}
```

Call `store.refresh()` once on the client. It reads `GET {basePath}/auth/session` (cookie or stored bearer token) and shows a saved session while it waits. `store.signIn(identifier, password)` and `store.signUp(identifier, password, name)` post to `/auth/username/sign-in` and `/auth/username/sign-up` by default and return `{ success: true }` or `{ success: false, error }`. `store.signOut()` clears local state, then revokes the session with `POST {basePath}/auth/sign-out`. To refetch on focus or an interval, pass `refetch` to `createSessionStore`, see [Session refetch and SSR](/client-sdk#session-refetch-and-ssr). `createSolidAuth` also returns `refresh` and `hydrateSession`. The store uses `fetch` only, so it runs in browsers, workers and edge runtimes. Without a `storage`, the session lives in memory only.

## What was run

The `lib/auth.ts` code type checks under `strict` against solid-js 1.x types and runs under `createRoot` in Node. Store behavior is covered by `packages/client/tests/session-store-solid.test.ts`. No browser run of the JSX.

# Expo / React Native

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/expo

`@glinr/theauth-expo` brings theAuth auth to React Native and Expo apps. It stores session tokens in any storage adapter you choose. AsyncStorage, SecureStore, or your own, and sends them via `Authorization` header rather than cookies.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @glinr/theauth-expo
# or
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-expo
```

You also need a storage library. The most common choices:

```bash
npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage
# or for encrypted storage
npx expo install expo-secure-store
```

## Setup

<Steps>
<Step>
### Wrap your app

```tsx
// app/_layout.tsx (Expo Router) or App.tsx
import { TheAuthExpoProvider } from '@glinr/theauth-expo';
import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage';

export default function RootLayout() {
  return (
    <TheAuthExpoProvider
      config={{
        basePath: 'https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth',
        storage: AsyncStorage,
      }}
    >
      <Stack />
    </TheAuthExpoProvider>
  );
}
```

The `storage` prop accepts any object with `getItem`, `setItem`, and `removeItem` methods, the same interface as `AsyncStorage` and `expo-secure-store`.
</Step>

<Step>
### Use the hooks

```tsx
import { useSignIn, useUser } from '@glinr/theauth-expo';

export function LoginScreen() {
  const { signIn, isLoading, error } = useSignIn();

  async function handleLogin() {
    const result = await signIn('user@example.com', 'password');
    if (result.success) {
      router.replace('/home');
    }
  }

  return (
    <View>
      <Button onPress={handleLogin} disabled={isLoading} title="Sign in" />
      {error && <Text>{error}</Text>}
    </View>
  );
}
```
</Step>
</Steps>

## Secure token storage

For production apps, use `expo-secure-store` to keep the session token in the Keychain (iOS) or Keystore (Android):

```tsx
import * as SecureStore from 'expo-secure-store';
import { TheAuthExpoProvider, createSecureStoreStorage } from '@glinr/theauth-expo';

<TheAuthExpoProvider
  config={{ basePath: 'https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth', storage: createSecureStoreStorage(SecureStore) }}
>
  {children}
</TheAuthExpoProvider>
```

## Social sign-in

The app opens the provider in the system browser, and the server sends the browser back to your app with a single-use code. The app trades that code, together with a PKCE verifier that never left the device, for a session. The session token is never placed in a URL.

<Steps>
<Step title="Allow your app's redirect URI on the server">
```typescript
oauth({
  providers: { github: github({ clientId, clientSecret }) },
  mobile: { redirectUris: ['myapp://auth/callback'] },
})
```
Matching is exact. Without `mobile`, the mobile flow is off.
</Step>
<Step title="Configure the provider in the app">
```tsx
import * as WebBrowser from 'expo-web-browser';
import * as Crypto from 'expo-crypto';
import * as Linking from 'expo-linking';
import { AppState } from 'react-native';

const config = {
  basePath: 'https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth',
  storage: createSecureStoreStorage(SecureStore),
  appState: AppState,
  social: {
    redirectUri: Linking.createURL('auth/callback'),
    openAuthSession: (url, redirectUri) => WebBrowser.openAuthSessionAsync(url, redirectUri),
    randomBytes: (n) => Crypto.getRandomBytesAsync(n),
    sha256: async (input) =>
      new Uint8Array(
        await Crypto.digest(Crypto.CryptoDigestAlgorithm.SHA256, new TextEncoder().encode(input)),
      ),
  },
};
```
</Step>
<Step title="Call the hook">
```tsx
import { useSocialSignIn } from '@glinr/theauth-expo';

const { signInWithProvider, isLoading, error } = useSocialSignIn();
<Button title="Continue with GitHub" onPress={() => signInWithProvider('github')} />
```
</Step>
</Steps>

If the user has a required second factor, `signInWithProvider` returns a failure whose message names the gate (`two_factor_required`). Complete the factor, then sign in again.

The mount path in `basePath` must expose the OAuth plugin routes `/auth/oauth/authorize/:provider` and `/auth/oauth/mobile/exchange`. The OAuth provider's own redirect URI stays your server callback, not the app link.

### Refresh on foreground

Pass React Native's `AppState` as `appState` and the session is re-checked every time the app comes back to the foreground, so a session revoked elsewhere signs the user out.

## Passkeys

Pass a platform authenticator and the provider can sign users in with a passkey and add one to a signed-in account. The server's passkey routes already return WebAuthn JSON options and a session token, so [`react-native-passkey`](https://github.com/f-23/react-native-passkey) works as is:

```tsx
import { Passkey } from 'react-native-passkey';
import { usePasskeys } from '@glinr/theauth-expo';

const config = { basePath: '...', passkeys: Passkey };

const { signInWithPasskey, registerPasskey, isLoading, error } = usePasskeys();
<Button title="Sign in with a passkey" onPress={() => signInWithPasskey()} />
<Button title="Add a passkey" onPress={() => registerPasskey('My phone')} />
```

`registerPasskey` needs a session, so call it after another sign-in method. Your app's associated domains (iOS) and Digital Asset Links (Android) must list the relying party ID the server uses. A required second factor comes back as a failure naming the gate, the same as social sign-in.

## Custom fetch (DPoP, pinning)

Every request the provider makes goes through `config.fetch` when set. Pass a DPoP client's `fetch` from `@glinr/theauth-client` to attach proofs, or your own pinned-certificate implementation:

```tsx
import { createDPoPClient } from '@glinr/theauth-client';

const dpop = createDPoPClient({ keyPair });   // needs a WebCrypto implementation
const config = { basePath: '...', fetch: dpop.fetch };
```

React Native has no `crypto.subtle` by default, so supply one (for example `react-native-quick-crypto`) and generate the key pair with it. Session tokens are plain bearer tokens on the server today, so proofs are useful for OAuth and MCP access tokens you also send through this fetch.

## Hooks reference

### `useSession`

```tsx
const { session, isLoading, refresh } = useSession();
```

### `useUser`

```tsx
const { user, isLoading, isAuthenticated } = useUser();
```

### `useSignIn`

```tsx
const { signIn, isLoading, error } = useSignIn();
const result = await signIn(email, password);
```

### `useSignUp`

```tsx
const { signUp, isLoading, error } = useSignUp();
const result = await signUp(email, password, name);
```

### `useSignOut`

```tsx
const { signOut } = useSignOut();
await signOut(); // clears stored token and calls server sign-out
```

### `useAgents`

```tsx
const { agents, create, revoke, rotate, isLoading, error } = useAgents(basePath);
```

Manages agent identity records for the current user. Requires the full base URL (same as the provider config).

## `AuthExpoConfig`

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `basePath` | `string` | Full URL to your theAuth mount point |
| `storage` | `AuthStorage?` | Token persistence adapter. Defaults to in-memory |
| `social` | `SocialSignInConfig?` | Enables `signInWithProvider`. See Social sign-in |
| `appState` | `AppStateLike?` | React Native `AppState`. Refreshes the session on foreground |
| `passkeys` | `PasskeyAuthenticator?` | Enables `signInWithPasskey` and `registerPasskey` |
| `fetch` | `typeof fetch?` | Used for every request, for DPoP or certificate pinning |

<Warning>
The default in-memory storage loses the session when the app restarts. Always pass a real storage adapter in production.
</Warning>

# Go SDK

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/sdk-go

`github.com/glincker/theauth-go` is the Go client for a theAuth server. It talks to the same REST API as `@glinr/theauth-client`. This is a client, not the Go server library.

## Installation

```bash
go get github.com/glincker/theauth-go
```

Requires Go 1.21 or newer. No external dependencies.

## Create a client

```go
client := theauth.NewClient("https://your-app.com/api/theauth",
    theauth.WithToken("ta_..."),
    theauth.WithTimeout(10*time.Second),
)
```

Every method takes a `context.Context` first and returns typed errors.

## Agents and authorization

```go
agent, err := client.Agents.Create(ctx, theauth.CreateAgentInput{
    OwnerID: "user-123",
    Name:    "github-reader",
    Type:    theauth.AgentTypeAutonomous,
})

result, err := client.Authorize(ctx, agent.ID, theauth.AuthorizeRequest{
    Action:   "read",
    Resource: "mcp:github:repos",
})
```

Delegation, audit and human auth live on `client.Delegation`, `client.Audit` and `client.Auth`.

## MCP servers

```go
srv, err := client.MCP.Register(ctx, theauth.RegisterMcpServerInput{
    Name:     "github",
    Endpoint: "https://mcp.example.com",
    Tools:    []string{"read_repo"},
})
servers, err := client.MCP.List(ctx)
found, err := client.MCP.Get(ctx, srv.ID) // nil, nil when missing
```

## Plugin endpoints

Call routes declared with `defineEndpoint` on the Go server. The path below is an example of a route you define yourself, not one the library ships. This client talks to the Go server only: the TypeScript handler serves a different route set (see [REST API](/api)).

```go
var out struct{ ID string `json:"id"` }
err := client.Request(ctx, theauth.RequestOptions{
    Method: "POST",
    Path:   "/auth/team/:teamId/invite",
    Params: map[string]string{"teamId": "t1"},
    Body:   map[string]string{"email": "a@b.c"},
}, &out)
```

`client.Do(ctx, method, path, query, body, &out)` is the short form without path parameters.

## Devices

`client.Devices` is the registry and needs a user or admin token. `client.Device` is what a device calls as itself.

```go
signer, _ := theauth.NewDeviceAssertionSigner("") // the key first, the id after registering
spec, _ := theauth.JWKCredential(signer.PublicJWK())
reg, err := client.Devices.Register(ctx, theauth.RegisterDeviceInput{
    OwnerID:     "user-123",
    Name:        "Pump 4",
    Permissions: []theauth.Permission{{Resource: "mqtt:plant/a/pump4/#", Actions: []string{"publish"}}},
    Credential:  &spec,
})
_ = signer.Bind(reg.Device.ID)

res, err := client.Device.Authorize(ctx, signer, theauth.AuthorizeRequest{
    Action: "publish", Resource: "mqtt:plant/a/pump4/temp",
})
```

The signer makes a new `device-assertion+jwt` for every call, because the server accepts each `jti` once. A `DevicePSK` or `DeviceToken` works as the credential too.

## Step-up and bound tokens

A 401 with `error="insufficient_user_authentication"` (RFC 9470) returns `*theauth.ErrStepUpRequired`. `err.Challenge.AuthorizeParams()` gives the `acr_values` and `max_age` for the new authorization request. `ACRSatisfies` and `AuthIsFresh` check a token before you call.

Set `Cnf: theauth.DPoPConfirmation(prover)` on `CreateAgentInput` to bind an agent token to a DPoP key (RFC 7800). `Agents.Rotate` keeps the binding and `Agents.RotateWith(ctx, id, theauth.RotateOptions{Unbind: true})` removes it. `AuthorizeRequest.Inputs` records what the model had in context for the audit log; the server hashes the content and does not store it.

## Errors

| Check | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `theauth.IsNotFound(err)` | 404 |
| `theauth.IsAuthentication(err)` | 401 |
| `theauth.IsPermission(err)` | 403 |
| `theauth.IsCSRFRejected(err)` | 403 with code `CSRF_REJECTED` |
| `theauth.IsRateLimited(err)` | 429, returns `Retry-After` seconds |
| `theauth.ValidationIssues(err)` | `issues` from a plugin endpoint validation failure |

All error types embed `TheAuthError` with `Code`, `Message`, `StatusCode`, `Details` and `Issues`.

## DPoP

Bind tokens to a key with RFC 9449 proofs. The prover uses the standard library only (ECDSA P-256, ES256).

```go
prover, err := theauth.NewDPoPProver()
client.UseDPoP(prover)
```

Each request carries a `DPoP` proof with `htm`, `htu` (no query or fragment), `iat`, `jti` and `ath` when a token is sent. A Bearer token is sent as `Authorization: DPoP <token>`. The `DPoP-Nonce` header is cached per origin and a `use_dpop_nonce` challenge is retried once.

To wrap your own `http.Client`:

```go
hc := theauth.DPoPHTTPClient(http.DefaultClient, prover)
thumbprint := prover.Thumbprint() // jkt
```

# Python SDK

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/sdk-python

The `theauth` package is the Python client for the theAuth REST API. It is built on `httpx` and ships a sync client and an async client with the same surface. Python 3.9 or newer.

## Installation

```bash
pip install theauth
# with DPoP support
pip install "theauth[dpop]"
```

## Create a client

```python
from theauth import TheAuthClient, TheAuthSyncClient

# async
async with TheAuthClient(base_url="https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth", token="ta_...") as client:
    agents = await client.agents.list()

# sync
with TheAuthSyncClient(base_url="https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth", token="ta_...") as client:
    agents = client.agents.list()
```

| Option | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | `str` | Mount point of theAuth on your server |
| `token` | `str?` | Bearer token sent on every request |
| `headers` | `dict?` | Extra headers on every request |
| `timeout` | `float` | Request timeout in seconds. Default 30 |
| `auth` | `httpx.Auth?` | Custom auth flow, for example `DPoPAuth` |

## Resources

| Resource | Methods |
|---|---|
| `client.agents` | `create`, `list`, `get`, `update`, `revoke`, `rotate`, `authorize` |
| `client.delegation` | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `get_effective_permissions` |
| `client.audit` | `query`, `query_paginated`, `export` |
| `client.mcp` | `register`, `list`, `get` |
| `client.auth` | `sign_up`, `sign_in`, `get_session`, `sign_out` |

## MCP servers

```python
from theauth.types import RegisterMcpServerInput

server = await client.mcp.register(
    RegisterMcpServerInput(
        name="github-mcp",
        endpoint="https://mcp.github.com",
        tools=["read_file", "list_repos"],
        rate_limit_rpm=60,
    )
)
found = await client.mcp.get(server.id)  # None when it does not exist
```

## Plugin routes

Call routes declared with `defineEndpoint` through `request()`. It returns the parsed JSON body.

```python
from theauth import ValidationError

try:
    result = await client.request(
        "POST", "/auth/team/invite", json={"email": "a@b.c"}
    )
except ValidationError as err:
    print(err.issues)
```

Validation failures raise `ValidationError` with the server `issues`. A 403 `CSRF_REJECTED` raises `PermissionError`, and a 429 raises `RateLimitError` with `retry_after`.

## DPoP

`DPoPAuth` signs each request with an ES256 key pair, as described in RFC 9449.

```python
from theauth import TheAuthSyncClient
from theauth.dpop import DPoPAuth

auth = DPoPAuth()
jkt = auth.thumbprint()  # bind your access token to this value

with TheAuthSyncClient(base_url=BASE, token=access_token, auth=auth) as client:
    client.agents.list()
```

- The `Authorization` header becomes `DPoP <token>` and the proof carries an `ath` claim.
- `htu` drops the query and fragment.
- The server `DPoP-Nonce` is cached per origin and a `use_dpop_nonce` response is retried once.

<Note>
`DPoPAuth` is a plain `httpx.Auth`, so you can also pass it to your own `httpx.Client` or `httpx.AsyncClient`. The `cryptography` package is imported lazily and a clear error is raised if it is missing.
</Note>

## Devices

`client.devices` is the registry and needs a user or admin token. `client.device` is what a device calls as itself: enroll, authorize, fetch an offline policy bundle.

```python
from theauth import (
    CredentialSpec, DeviceAssertionSigner, RegisterDeviceInput, TheAuthSyncClient,
)
from theauth.types import AuthorizeRequest, Permission

signer = DeviceAssertionSigner()  # the key first, the id after registering
with TheAuthSyncClient(base_url=BASE, token=admin_token) as client:
    reg = client.devices.register(
        RegisterDeviceInput(
            owner_id="user-123",
            name="Pump 4",
            permissions=[Permission("mqtt:plant/a/pump4/#", ["publish"])],
            credential=CredentialSpec.from_jwk(signer.public_jwk),
        )
    )
    signer.bind(reg.device.id)
    result = client.device.authorize(signer, AuthorizeRequest("publish", "mqtt:plant/a/pump4/temp"))
    client.devices.suspend(reg.device.id, "stolen")
```

`DeviceAssertionSigner` signs the `device-assertion+jwt` the server verifies. It makes a new assertion for every call because the server accepts each `jti` once. It needs the `cryptography` extra, like DPoP.

## Step-up

A 401 with `error="insufficient_user_authentication"` (RFC 9470) raises `StepUpRequiredError`, a subclass of `AuthenticationError`. `error.challenge.authorize_params()` gives the `acr_values` and `max_age` for the new authorization request.

```python
from theauth import StepUpRequiredError

try:
    client.approvals.approve(approval_id)
except StepUpRequiredError as err:
    print(err.challenge.authorize_params() if err.challenge else {})
```

`acr_satisfies` and `auth_is_fresh` check a token's `acr` and `auth_time` before you call.

## Bound tokens and input provenance

Pass `cnf=dpop_confirmation(prover)` to `CreateAgentInput` to bind an agent token to a DPoP key (RFC 7800). `client.agents.rotate(id)` keeps the binding, `rotate(id, cnf=None)` removes it. `AuthorizeRequest(inputs=[ProvenanceInput("user_message", content=text)])` records what the model had in context; the server hashes the content and does not store it.

## Errors

All exceptions inherit from `TheAuthError` and carry `code`, `message` and `status_code`.

| Class | When |
|---|---|
| `AuthenticationError` | 401 |
| `StepUpRequiredError` | 401 with a step-up challenge, has `challenge` |
| `PermissionError` | 403 |
| `NotFoundError` | 404 |
| `ValidationError` | 400 or 422 with `issues` |
| `RateLimitError` | 429, has `retry_after` |
| `ServerError` | 5xx |
| `NetworkError` | Transport failure |

  </Card>

# Electron

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/electron

`@glinr/theauth-electron` provides secure auth for Electron desktop apps with encrypted token storage, OAuth popup windows, and an IPC bridge for renderer-to-main communication.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-electron
```

## Setup (main process)

Create a storage adapter backed by Electron's `safeStorage` API, then expose it to the renderer over IPC:

```ts
import { app, ipcMain } from 'electron';
import { createElectronStorage, setupTheAuthIpc } from '@glinr/theauth-electron';

const storage = createElectronStorage({ fileName: 'theauth-session.json' });
setupTheAuthIpc(storage);
```

Open the OAuth popup window from a main-process IPC handler:

```ts
import { ipcMain } from 'electron';
import { openOAuthWindow } from '@glinr/theauth-electron';

ipcMain.handle('theauth:sign-in-oauth', async (_event, providerId: string) => {
  return openOAuthWindow(providerId, { basePath: 'https://api.myapp.com/api/theauth' });
});
```

## Usage (renderer)

Wrap your renderer's React tree in `ElectronTheAuthProvider`. Pass a `SecureStorage` adapter, either `createIpcStorage()` (delegates to the main process over IPC, recommended with `contextIsolation`) or `createElectronStorage()` directly if Node integration is enabled:

```tsx
import { ElectronTheAuthProvider, createIpcStorage } from '@glinr/theauth-electron';

const storage = createIpcStorage();

export function App() {
  return (
    <ElectronTheAuthProvider basePath="/api/theauth" storage={storage}>
      <SignedInView />
    </ElectronTheAuthProvider>
  );
}
```

Read session state and call auth actions with `useElectronTheAuthContext`:

```tsx
import { useElectronTheAuthContext } from '@glinr/theauth-electron';

function SignedInView() {
  const { session, user, isLoading, isAuthenticated, signIn, signOut, refresh } =
    useElectronTheAuthContext();

  if (isLoading) return <p>Loading...</p>;
  if (!isAuthenticated) {
    return (
      <button onClick={() => signIn('alice@example.com', 'password')}>
        Sign in
      </button>
    );
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <p>Signed in as {user?.email}</p>
      <button onClick={signOut}>Sign out</button>
    </div>
  );
}
```

`signIn` and `signUp` authenticate against the email/password endpoints on your theAuth API. For OAuth providers, trigger `openOAuthWindow` from the main process (see above), then call `refresh()` from the renderer once the window resolves to pick up the new session.

## Features

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| Secure storage | Tokens encrypted via Electron's `safeStorage` API |
| OAuth popup | Opens provider auth in a new `BrowserWindow` |
| IPC bridge | Secure main/renderer communication via `setupTheAuthIpc` / `createIpcStorage` |
| Session persistence | `ElectronTheAuthProvider` restores and re-verifies sessions on launch |

<Info>
Token storage uses Electron's `safeStorage.encryptString()` which uses the OS keychain (Keychain on macOS, DPAPI on Windows, Secret Service on Linux). If encryption is unavailable, `createElectronStorage` falls back to plaintext and logs a warning.
</Info>

# Browser extensions

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/browser-extension

`@glinr/theauth-extension` signs a user into your extension against a TheAuth authorization server, using the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256). It keeps the access token fresh across service worker restarts and gives content scripts and popups a way to ask the background for a token without ever seeing the refresh token.

It has no runtime dependencies. DPoP support uses `@glinr/theauth-client`, which is an optional peer.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-extension
# only for DPoP
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-client
```

The package ships ES modules. Bundle it into your background script with whatever bundler you already use (esbuild, Vite, webpack). Extensions cannot load code from a CDN under Manifest V3.

## Manifest permissions

```json
{
  "manifest_version": 3,
  "name": "My extension",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "permissions": ["identity", "storage"],
  "background": { "service_worker": "background.js", "type": "module" },
  "action": { "default_popup": "popup.html" }
}
```

- `identity` is needed for `identity.launchWebAuthFlow` and `identity.getRedirectURL`.
- `storage` is needed for `storage.local` and `storage.session`.

No host permission is required for the sign in itself. Calls from the background to your authorization server and API are subject to that server's CORS policy unless you add `host_permissions` for it.

## Register the redirect URI

`identity.getRedirectURL()` returns a URL on a browser-controlled domain. On Chrome it looks like `https://<extension-id>.chromiumapp.org/`. Register exactly that value as a redirect URI for your OAuth client:

```ts
// Evaluate this in the background console, then register the value.
chrome.identity.getRedirectURL();
```

The extension id changes between an unpacked build and the Web Store build unless you pin it with a `key` in the manifest. Register each redirect URI you use, or pin the key.

Register the client as a public client (`token_endpoint_auth_method: "none"`) with the `authorization_code` and `refresh_token` grants. An extension cannot keep a client secret.

## Background script

```ts
import {
  createExtensionAuth,
  exposeAuthToBackground,
} from "@glinr/theauth-extension";

const auth = createExtensionAuth({
  issuer: "https://auth.example.com",
  clientId: "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  scopes: ["openid", "profile", "offline_access", "mcp:read"],
  resource: "https://mcp.example.com",
  encryptRefreshToken: true,
});

// Answer popups and content scripts. Register at the top level of the
// worker so the listener exists when the worker wakes for a message.
exposeAuthToBackground(auth);

auth.onChange((session) => {
  chrome.action.setBadgeText({ text: session ? "on" : "" });
});
```

Create the auth object at the top level of the service worker, not inside an event handler. Every wakeup runs the script again, builds a new object and reads its state from storage.

`createExtensionAuth` options:

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `issuer` | none | Discovery at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414). The metadata `issuer` must match. |
| `endpoints` | none | `{ authorization, token, revocation?, endSession?, issuer?, issuerParameterSupported? }`. Skips discovery. |
| `clientId`, `scopes` | required | |
| `resource` | none | RFC 8707 indicator, sent on authorize, token and refresh requests. |
| `redirectUri` | `identity.getRedirectURL()` | |
| `storage`, `identity`, `fetch`, `clock` | `browser` or `chrome`, `Date.now` | Injectable, mostly for tests. |
| `encryptRefreshToken` | `false` | AES-GCM with a non-extractable key in IndexedDB. |
| `dpop` | `false` | `true`, or `{ module }`. See below. |
| `refreshSkewSeconds` | `60` | Refresh this long before expiry. |
| `endSession` | `false` | Navigate `end_session_endpoint` on sign out when advertised. |

Returned object: `signIn()`, `getAccessToken()`, `getSession()`, `signOut()`, `onChange(cb)` and `fetch(url, init)`. `fetch` attaches the right `Authorization` scheme, refreshes first when needed and handles DPoP nonce challenges.

## Popup and content script

```ts
import { createAuthClient } from "@glinr/theauth-extension";

const auth = createAuthClient();

// popup.ts
document.querySelector("#sign-in")?.addEventListener("click", async () => {
  await auth.signIn();
});

// content-script.ts
const token = await auth.getAccessToken();
const res = await fetch("https://mcp.example.com/tools", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` },
});
```

Content scripts can call `getAccessToken` and `getSession`. `signIn` and `signOut` are accepted only from extension pages such as the popup and options page, because a content script runs next to untrusted page content. If you enabled DPoP, do not call the resource from a content script with the token alone: do the request in the background with `auth.fetch`, since the key never leaves it.

Sender checks:

- A message must carry `sender.id` equal to the extension's own id. Anything else is answered with a `message_rejected` error.
- Messages from other extensions arrive on `runtime.onMessageExternal`. That listener is registered only when you pass `allowedExtensionIds`, and only those ids are served.
- `senderFilter(sender, method)` lets you add your own rule, for example to restrict content scripts to specific origins.

## Errors

Every method throws `ExtensionAuthError` with a `code`:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `user_cancelled` | The user closed the window or denied access. |
| `state_mismatch` | The `state` on the redirect was missing or wrong. |
| `discovery_failed` | Metadata was unreachable, malformed or named another issuer. |
| `authorization_failed` | The server returned an error, or `iss` was wrong or missing. |
| `token_exchange_failed` | The code exchange was rejected, or the ID token nonce was wrong. |
| `refresh_failed` | Refresh was rejected or the stored refresh token failed its integrity check. |
| `not_signed_in` | There is no session. |
| `invalid_config` | Missing storage or identity API, or DPoP could not load. |
| `message_rejected` | A message sender or method was not allowed. |

On `invalid_grant` from the token endpoint the package clears all stored state, calls `onChange(null)` and throws `refresh_failed`. Transient failures (network, 5xx) keep the state so the next call can retry.

## Storage and the refresh token

| Item | Where | Lifetime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Access token, expiry, ID token | `storage.session` | Until the browser session ends |
| Refresh token | `storage.local` | Until sign out or `invalid_grant` |
| Refresh lock | `storage.local` | Expires after 30 seconds |
| DPoP key pair, seal key | IndexedDB, non-extractable | Until site data is cleared |

If `storage.session` does not exist in the browser, the access token is held in memory only and the worker refreshes after each restart.

With `encryptRefreshToken: true` the refresh token is sealed with AES-GCM before it is written. The key is a non-extractable `CryptoKey` kept in IndexedDB, and the ciphertext is bound to its storage slot, so a value copied to another key fails to open and a modified value is rejected before any request is sent.

This is defence in depth, not a vault. Extension storage and IndexedDB are readable by your extension's own code, and so by anything that compromises it, including a supply chain attack on one of your dependencies. A non-extractable key stops that code from copying the key bytes, but it can still ask the browser to decrypt. What the sealing does protect against is disk-level reads of the profile, backup and sync tools that copy `storage.local`, and bugs that leak the storage object. Keep refresh token lifetimes short, rotate them on use and turn on revocation on the server.

## Refresh in a service worker

The worker can be stopped at any time and two copies of your code can briefly overlap (a popup page importing the same module, or a wakeup racing a shutdown). The package handles this in two layers:

1. An in-memory promise, so concurrent callers in one worker share one refresh.
2. A lock record in `storage.local` with an expiry, so a second instance waits for the first and then reads the new tokens instead of spending the refresh token again.

The extension storage API has no compare-and-set, so the lock is write then read back. Two contexts that write in the same instant can both believe they hold it. With refresh token rotation the loser gets `invalid_grant` and the user is signed out. Servers that allow a short grace period for a just-rotated token avoid this. The expiry means a worker killed mid-refresh does not block sign in for more than `lockTtlMs`.

A worker killed during the interactive sign in window loses the pending sign in. The user sees `user_cancelled` or nothing, and starts again.

## DPoP

```ts
import * as client from "@glinr/theauth-client";

const auth = createExtensionAuth({
  issuer: "https://auth.example.com",
  clientId: "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  scopes: ["mcp:read", "offline_access"],
  dpop: { module: client },
});

const res = await auth.fetch("https://mcp.example.com/tools");
```

An ES256 key pair is generated with a non-extractable private key and stored in IndexedDB, so the same key is used after a restart. Token and refresh requests carry a `DPoP` proof, resource requests made through `auth.fetch` get `Authorization: DPoP <token>` with a proof bound to the token (`ath`), and a `use_dpop_nonce` challenge is retried once.

Pass the module yourself when you bundle the worker. With `dpop: true` the package falls back to a dynamic `import()` of `@glinr/theauth-client`, which service workers do not allow. See [DPoP and requireMcpAuth](/dpop) for the server side.

## Sign out

`signOut()` posts the refresh token to the revocation endpoint when the server advertises one (RFC 7009), clears storage, emits `null` and returns `{ revoked }`. A failed revocation does not stop the local sign out. With `endSession: true` it also loads `end_session_endpoint` with `id_token_hint` and `post_logout_redirect_uri` set to the extension redirect URL, without showing a window.

## Browser support

Tested here: the package against fake `identity` and `storage` objects in Node, and against the in-process MCP authorization server from `@glinr/theauth`. It has not been run inside a real browser yet.

- Chrome and other Chromium browsers (Edge, Brave): the API shape comes from the Chrome documentation. UNVERIFIED in a live browser.
- Firefox: `identity.launchWebAuthFlow` and `storage.session` exist (the latter from Firefox 115), and its redirect URL is on `extensions.allizom.org` with a value derived from `browser_specific_settings.gecko.id`, so set that id. Firefox runs Manifest V3 background code as an event page rather than a service worker. UNVERIFIED.
- Safari: We believe Safari web extensions do not provide `identity.launchWebAuthFlow`. If that holds, pass your own `identity` object (the `identity` option takes any object with `launchWebAuthFlow` and `getRedirectURL`) backed by a tab or a native bridge. UNVERIFIED.
- Chrome returns a rejected promise with the text "The user did not approve access." when the window is closed. The package treats messages matching cancel, closed, dismiss, denied or "did not approve" as `user_cancelled`. Other browsers word this differently and may surface as `authorization_failed`.

## Limits

- The access token is readable by any code in the extension background. There is no hardware backing for the refresh token.
- `onChange` fires inside the context that made the change. Other contexts learn about a sign out on their next call, which will fail with `not_signed_in`.
- ID token claims are decoded without verifying the signature. The token is received directly from the token endpoint over TLS and its `nonce` is checked, which is what OpenID Connect Core allows. Do not forward the ID token to another service as proof of identity.
- Sign in needs `identity.launchWebAuthFlow`, which opens a browser-managed window. It does not work in a headless profile.

---

# UI components

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/ui-components

`@glinr/theauth-ui` provides drop-in React components for auth flows. Each component renders inside `TheAuthProvider` from `@glinr/theauth-react` and wires up to your theAuth API route automatically, no manual fetch calls required.

<Info>
  Components require `@glinr/theauth-react` to be installed and a `TheAuthProvider` wrapping your app. See the [React hooks](/react) page for provider setup.
</Info>

## Installation

```bash
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-ui
```

Components are unstyled by default and rely on Tailwind CSS for layout and spacing. Add `@glinr/theauth-ui` to your `tailwind.config.ts` content paths:

```ts
// tailwind.config.ts
export default {
  content: [
    './src/**/*.{ts,tsx}',
    './node_modules/@glinr/theauth-ui/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}',
  ],
};
```

## Copy the source into your project

If you want to own and edit the components rather than depend on the package, copy them in, the way shadcn/ui works. This is optional: the packaged components keep working and you can mix both.

```bash
npx @glinr/theauth-cli add sign-in
```

The command writes plain TSX into `src/components/theauth` (or `components/theauth` when there is no `src` folder), prints the one dependency to install, and never overwrites a file you changed unless you pass `--overwrite`. Each component pulls in `theauth-base` (types, class helper, default slots and the auth card) once.

```bash
theauth add --list                       # sign-in, sign-up, forgot-password, ...
theauth add sign-in sign-up              # several at once
theauth add sign-in --dir app/ui/auth    # choose the folder
theauth add sign-in --dry-run            # show what would be written
```

The same items are published in the shadcn registry format, so the shadcn CLI works too:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-in.json
```

Then import from the copied folder and keep wiring through `TheAuthProvider` as above:

```tsx
import { SignIn } from "@/components/theauth/sign-in";
```

Copied files import `@glinr/theauth-react` for the hooks and nothing else beyond React. Re-run `theauth add <name> --overwrite` after upgrading if you want the newer upstream version, and review the diff first.

## Available components

| Component | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `SignIn` | Email/password and magic-link sign-in form |
| `SignUp` | New account registration form |
| `UserButton` | Avatar dropdown with sign-out and custom menu items |
| `ForgotPassword` | Password reset request form |
| `TwoFactorVerify` | TOTP/backup-code entry for 2FA flows |
| `OAuthButtons` | Social login buttons (Google, GitHub, Discord, and more) |
| `AuthCard` | Generic card shell for building custom auth pages |

## SignIn

Renders an email/password form. Pass `showMagicLink` to add a passwordless tab. Pass `providers` to show OAuth buttons above the form.

```tsx
import { SignIn } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';
import { OAUTH_PROVIDERS } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';

export default function LoginPage() {
  return (
    <SignIn
      providers={[OAUTH_PROVIDERS.google, OAUTH_PROVIDERS.github]}
      showMagicLink
      signUpUrl="/sign-up"
      forgotPasswordUrl="/forgot-password"
      onSuccess={() => window.location.href = '/dashboard'}
    />
  );
}
```

<ParamField path="providers" type="OAuthProviderMeta[]" default="[]">OAuth providers to show above the form.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="showMagicLink" type="boolean" default="false">Add a magic-link tab alongside password sign-in.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signUpUrl" type="string">URL for the "Sign up" link in the footer.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="forgotPasswordUrl" type="string">URL for the "Forgot password?" link.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="() => void">Called on successful sign-in.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="title" type="string" default="&quot;Sign in&quot;">Heading text.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="basePath" type="string" default="&quot;/api/theauth&quot;">Must match your theAuth API route.</ParamField>

## SignUp

```tsx
import { SignUp } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';

export default function RegisterPage() {

    <SignUp

```

<ParamField path="showName" type="boolean" default="false">Include a name field.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="confirmPassword" type="boolean" default="false">Add a confirm-password field.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="signInUrl" type="string">URL for the "Sign in" link.</ParamField>
<ParamField path="onSuccess" type="() => void">Called on successful registration.</ParamField>

## UserButton

Renders an avatar that opens a dropdown menu. Includes sign-out by default. Pass `menuItems` to add custom actions.

```tsx
import { UserButton } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';

export default function Nav() {
  return (
    <UserButton
      showEmail
      menuItems={[
        { label: 'Settings', onClick: () => router.push('/settings') },
        { label: 'Delete account', onClick: handleDelete, danger: true },
      ]}
      onSignOut={() => router.push('/sign-in')}
    />
  );
}
```

## OAuthButtons

Use standalone when you want social login without the full sign-in card.

```tsx
import { OAuthButtons, OAUTH_PROVIDERS } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';

<OAuthButtons
  providers={[
    OAUTH_PROVIDERS.google,
    OAUTH_PROVIDERS.github,
    OAUTH_PROVIDERS.discord,
  ]}
  mode="signin"
  layout="list"
/>
```

`OAUTH_PROVIDERS` ships with metadata and icons for Google, GitHub, GitLab, Discord, Twitter, Facebook, Microsoft, Apple, LinkedIn, Slack, Notion, Reddit, Spotify, and Twitch. You can also pass a custom provider object matching `OAuthProviderMeta`.

## Customization

### Class name overrides

Every component accepts a `classNames` prop with keys for each sub-element. Pass a string to append classes, or a function that receives the default class string.

```tsx
<SignIn
  classNames={{
    card: 'shadow-none border-0',
    button: (defaults) => `${defaults} bg-violet-600 hover:bg-violet-500`,
    input: 'rounded-none border-b border-zinc-300',
  }}
/>
```

### Slot replacement

Pass a `components` prop to replace any primitive (input, button, link, divider, error). Useful when you need to use your own design system components.

```tsx
import { SignIn } from '@glinr/theauth-ui';
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button';
import { Input } from '@/components/ui/input';

<SignIn
  components={{
    Button: ({ children, loading, ...props }) => (
      <Button {...props} disabled={loading}>{children}</Button>
    ),
    Input: ({ label, error, ...props }) => (
      <div>
        <label>{label}</label>
        <Input {...props} />
        {error && <p className="text-red-500 text-xs">{error}</p>}
      </div>
    ),
  }}
/>
```

The `cx` utility is exported from `@glinr/theauth-ui` for merging class names in your own slot components.

# UI headless

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/ui-headless

`@glinr/theauth-ui-headless` ships account components with behavior and accessibility built in and no visual styling. Every user-facing string comes from a required `labels` prop, and every part carries a `data-part` attribute plus an optional `classNames` slot, so you apply your own styles (Tailwind, CSS modules or anything else). If you want ready-made styling instead, use [UI components](/ui-components).

The package wraps the query hooks from `@glinr/theauth-react/query`, so it must render inside `TheAuthQueryProvider`.

<Warning>
  These components talk to the Go server, through `createTheAuthGoClient`. Its routes (`/auth/sessions`, `/auth/tokens`, `/auth/account/agents`, `/auth/step-up`, `/auth/device/approve`) are served by the Go server. The TypeScript handler does not serve them: it has `/auth/session`, `/agents`, `/auth/2fa/verify` and `/auth/passkey/step-up/*` instead. Point `baseUrl` at a Go server.
</Warning>

## What it includes

| Component | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `SessionList` | Lists the signed-in sessions, revokes one, or revokes all others. |
| `ApiTokenList` | Lists personal or agent API tokens and revokes them. |
| `MintTokenForm` | Creates a token with chosen abilities and expiry, and shows the secret once with a copy button. |
| `AgentList`, `AgentRegisterForm` | List agents and register a new one. |
| `DeviceApproval` | Approves or denies a device sign-in request (RFC 8628). |
| `StepUpDialog` and `useStepUpRetry` | Asks for a password, TOTP code or passkey when the server returns `auth.recent_auth_required`, then retries the blocked action. |

## Install

```bash title="terminal"
pnpm add @glinr/theauth-ui-headless @glinr/theauth-react @glinr/theauth-client @tanstack/react-query react
```

Peer dependencies are `react` (18 or newer), `@tanstack/react-query` (5 or newer), `@glinr/theauth-react` and `@glinr/theauth-client`. `npm install` and `yarn add` work the same way.

## Example

This page renders a session list. Clicks on revoke go through `useStepUpRetry`, so a revoke that needs fresh authentication opens the dialog and retries once the user confirms.

```tsx title="app/settings/sessions.tsx"
import { createTheAuthGoClient } from "@glinr/theauth-client";
import { TheAuthQueryProvider } from "@glinr/theauth-react/query";
import {
  SessionList,
  StepUpDialog,
  useStepUpRetry,
} from "@glinr/theauth-ui-headless";

const client = createTheAuthGoClient({
  baseUrl: "https://api.example.com",
  basePath: "/auth",
});

const sessionLabels = {
  title: "Active sessions",
  loading: "Loading sessions",
  empty: "No other sessions",
  current: "This device",
  revokeOthers: "Sign out other sessions",
  lastSeen: (iso: string) => `Last seen ${new Date(iso).toLocaleString()}`,
  revoke: () => "Sign out",
  error: (code: string) => `Something went wrong (${code})`,
};

const stepUpLabels = {
  title: "Confirm it is you",
  methods: { password: "Password", totp: "Authenticator code", passkey: "Passkey" },
  password: "Password",
  totpCode: "Code",
  passkeyPrompt: "Use your passkey to continue",
  submit: "Confirm",
  cancel: "Cancel",
  error: (code: string) => `Could not verify (${code})`,
};

export function SessionSettings() {
  const { run, dialogProps } = useStepUpRetry();

  return (
    <TheAuthQueryProvider client={client}>
      <SessionList
        labels={sessionLabels}
        run={run}
        classNames={{ item: "flex items-center gap-3 py-2", revoke: "text-sm text-red-600" }}
      />
      <StepUpDialog {...dialogProps} labels={stepUpLabels} />
    </TheAuthQueryProvider>
  );
}
```

`labels.error(code)` receives a stable code such as `invalid_expiry` or `invalid_credentials`, so map it to your own copy. Components also set `data-error-code` on the alert element, which is useful in tests.

## Related

- [UI components](/ui-components) for prebuilt, Tailwind-styled forms.
- [React](/react) for `TheAuthProvider` and the hooks these components use.
- [Client SDK](/client-sdk) for the typed client behind `createTheAuthGoClient`.

# Publish theAuth components and MCP server

Source: https://docs.theauth.dev/publishing

Install the React components with the shadcn CLI, or list the MCP server in the MCP Registry.

## Install a component

Run from your app root:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-in.json
```

Several at once:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-in.json \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-up.json
```

| Item | URL |
| --- | --- |
| `theauth-base` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/theauth-base.json` |
| `oauth-buttons` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/oauth-buttons.json` |
| `sign-in` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-in.json` |
| `sign-up` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/sign-up.json` |
| `forgot-password` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/forgot-password.json` |
| `two-factor-verify` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/two-factor-verify.json` |
| `user-button` | `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/glincker/theauth/main/registry/user-button.json` |

The CLI also installs `registryDependencies`, such as `theauth-base`. Files land in `components/theauth/`. Import from `@glinr/theauth-react` and wrap your app in `TheAuthProvider`. These are the items `theauth add` installs. For packaged versions, see [UI components](/ui-components).

## Rebuild the registry

After changing a component:

```bash
node scripts/build-registry.mjs
```

Each item carries its file text in `content`. Source: `packages/ui/src/components`. `registry/registry.json` is an index with no content, so do not pass it to `shadcn add`. To check that every item has content:

```bash
node -e "for (const f of require('fs').readdirSync('registry')) if (f !== 'registry.json') { const d = require('./registry/' + f); if (!d.files.every((x) => x.content)) throw new Error(f); }"
```

## Publish to the MCP Registry

The `@glinr/theauth-mcp` package ships `server.json` at `packages/mcp/server.json`. The Registry stores metadata only, so publish the npm package first.

| Field | Required value |
| --- | --- |
| `name` in `server.json` | `io.github.glincker/theauth-mcp` |
| `mcpName` in `packages/mcp/package.json` | Same as `name` |
| `version` (top level and `packages[0]`) | On npm (currently `1.1.1`). No ranges or `latest`. |
| `description` | At most 100 characters |
| `$schema` | `https://static.modelcontextprotocol.io/schemas/2025-12-11/server.schema.json` |

Bump both versions in `server.json` on every publish.

<Steps>

<Step>

### Publish the npm package

```bash
npm publish --access public
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Install mcp-publisher

```bash
brew install mcp-publisher
```

On Linux, download the release tarball from `https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry/releases/latest`.

</Step>

<Step>

### Validate

```bash
cd packages/mcp
mcp-publisher validate
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Log in

```bash
mcp-publisher login github
```

Open `https://github.com/login/device` and enter the code shown. You must be able to act for the `glincker` organization.

</Step>

<Step>

### Publish

```bash
mcp-publisher publish
```

</Step>

<Step>

### Confirm

```bash
curl "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=io.github.glincker/theauth-mcp"
```

</Step>

</Steps>

## Namespaces

| Namespace | How it is verified |
| --- | --- |
| `io.github.<user or org>/name` | `mcp-publisher login github` |
| `com.example/name` (reverse domain) | DNS TXT record or HTTP file, then `mcp-publisher login dns` or `login http` |

For a domain namespace, make an Ed25519 key and publish the public key as a TXT record on the apex (or serve `v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=<PUBLIC_KEY>` at `https://example.com/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth`):

```bash
openssl genpkey -algorithm Ed25519 -out key.pem
PUBLIC_KEY="$(openssl pkey -in key.pem -pubout -outform DER | tail -c 32 | base64)"
echo "example.com. IN TXT \"v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=${PUBLIC_KEY}\""
PRIVATE_KEY="$(openssl pkey -in key.pem -noout -text | grep -A3 "priv:" | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' :\n')"
mcp-publisher login dns --domain example.com --private-key "${PRIVATE_KEY}"
```

## Common errors

- "You do not have permission to publish this server": the `name` prefix does not match your login namespace.
- "Invalid or expired Registry JWT token": run `mcp-publisher login github` again.
- "Registry validation failed for package": `mcpName` is missing or differs from `name`, or the version is not on npm.

## Limits

- The Registry is in preview. Check its docs if a step fails.
- On macOS, use Homebrew OpenSSL 3. The system `openssl` cannot make Ed25519 keys.
- Changing the namespace means updating `name` and `mcpName` together.
